cards.front:
India's MAIN HOT DESERT, the THAR, lies primarily in:

(A) Punjab + Haryana states (north India)
(B) Rajasthan (and parts of Gujarat, Sindh)
(C) Madhya Pradesh + Chhattisgarh (central)
(D) Tamil Nadu + Kerala (south India coast)
cards.back:
(B) Rajasthan (and parts of Gujarat, Sindh)

Physical Features — THAR DESERT (also called GREAT INDIAN DESERT or MARUSTHALI) — covers ~200,000 sq km. Mostly RAJASTHAN (~60%), parts of GUJARAT (Kutch is partly desert), Pakistan (Sindh + Cholistan = ~80% of Thar in Pakistan side). 17th LARGEST desert in the world. INHA-INDIRA GANDHI CANAL (formerly Rajasthan canal) — brings water from Punjab rivers; helped agriculture in part of Thar. Climate: extreme — summer 50°C+; winter near freezing. Most population density of any desert — ~80 people/km² (Thar has historic towns: Jaisalmer, Bikaner, Jodhpur).

cards.front:
India's COLD DESERT region is in:

(A) Sundarbans of West Bengal coast
(B) Ladakh + Spiti valley (high altitude)
(C) Tamil Nadu coastal area near sea
(D) Kerala backwaters tropical region
cards.back:
(B) Ladakh + Spiti valley (high altitude)

Physical Features — COLD DESERT — LADAKH + LAHAUL-SPITI valley (Himachal). High altitude (3000-5500 m). RAINSHADOW of Himalayas + Karakoram → very dry (<200 mm rainfall). Cold (winter −30 to −40°C; summer ~25°C). Sparse vegetation. Famous: HEMIS National Park (Ladakh — snow leopard habitat), Pin Valley NP (Spiti — Himalayan ibex, red fox), Tso Moriri + Pangong lakes. PEOPLE: Ladakhis + Tibetans (ethnic + cultural similarity); Buddhist monasteries (Hemis, Thiksey, Diskit). Famous DOUBLE-HUMP CAMEL (Bactrian camel) — Nubra Valley, only place in India.
cards.option2: Tamil Nadu coastal area near sea

cards.front:
ARAVALI RANGE (one of the oldest mountain ranges in the world) acts as a barrier to the eastward spread of:

(A) Ganga river system in north
(B) Thar desert (eastward expansion)
(C) Brahmaputra river of north-east
(D) Himalayan glaciers melting flow
cards.back:
(B) Thar desert (eastward expansion)

Physical Features — ARAVALI — one of OLDEST fold mountain ranges in the world (~3.5 BILLION years!). Highly eroded. Stretches from Gujarat (Pavagadh) → Rajasthan → Haryana → Delhi → up to ~700 km. Highest peak: GURUSHIKHAR (1722 m, Mt Abu). Acts as a NATURAL BARRIER preventing eastward expansion of Thar desert into Indo-Gangetic plain. DEFORESTATION + mining (illegal) of Aravali → desert is creeping into Haryana/Delhi. Famous places along Aravali: MOUNT ABU (only hill station in Rajasthan), ALWAR, RANTHAMBORE, UDAIPUR (in Aravali foothills). Mining banned in NCR Aravali area by SC.

cards.front:
INDIRA GANDHI CANAL, longest canal in India, brings water to Thar desert from:

(A) Yamuna at Tajewala headworks (Haryana)
(B) Sutlej-Beas (HARIKE BARRAGE) in Punjab
(C) Ganga at Haridwar's main barrage works
(D) Narmada at Sardar Sarovar dam (Gujarat)
cards.back:
(B) Sutlej-Beas (HARIKE BARRAGE) in Punjab

Physical Features — INDIRA GANDHI CANAL (formerly Rajasthan Canal; renamed 1984 after PM's death). Source: HARIKE BARRAGE in Punjab (confluence of Sutlej + Beas). Length: ~650 km — longest canal in India. Built in stages from 1958. Brings water to NW Rajasthan (Bikaner, Sri Ganganagar, Hanumangarh, Jaisalmer, Barmer, Churu) — turned a desert into a wheat / mustard / cotton-growing region. Dependent on Indus Water Treaty (1960) — eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) granted to India. Critique: water-intensive irrigation in arid zone → waterlogging + salinity in some areas.
cards.option2: Ganga at Haridwar's main barrage works

cards.front:
The 'GREAT INDIAN BUSTARD' (critically endangered bird) is found in:

(A) Sundarbans of West Bengal
(B) Thar desert + Kutch grasslands
(C) Western Ghats rainforests
(D) Eastern Himalayas of Sikkim
cards.back:
(B) Thar desert + Kutch grasslands

Physical Features — GREAT INDIAN BUSTARD (Ardeotis nigriceps) — large-bodied (~1 m tall), brownish, ground-dwelling bird. State bird of Rajasthan. Habitat: arid + semi-arid GRASSLANDS of Thar (Rajasthan, esp. JAISALMER + DESERT NATIONAL PARK), Kutch (Gujarat — DABASIRI Sanctuary), Andhra/Maharashtra patches. CRITICALLY ENDANGERED — fewer than 150 left! Threats: habitat loss, electrocution from power lines (major cause; SC ordered transmission lines underground in some habitats), pesticides. Conservation: PROJECT GREAT INDIAN BUSTARD (Sariska + Desert NP, captive breeding at Sam, Jaisalmer). Known locally as GODAWAN.

cards.front:
RANN OF KUTCH is a unique ecosystem in:

(A) Maharashtra (around Konkan coast)
(B) Gujarat (large salt marsh on western coast)
(C) Rajasthan (around Jaisalmer area)
(D) Punjab (across Indo-Pak border)
cards.back:
(B) Gujarat (large salt marsh on western coast)

Physical Features — RANN OF KUTCH — vast salt marsh in KUTCH region of GUJARAT (NW India), borders Pakistan's Sindh. Two parts: GREAT RANN (~7500 sq km, north) + LITTLE RANN (~5000 sq km, south). One of largest SALT DESERTS in the world. Floods during monsoon (becomes shallow lake); turns to dazzling white salt flats in winter. Famous: WILD ASS (only home of Indian wild ass — Khur, Equus hemionus khur — in Little Rann). FLAMINGOS at Khadir Bet. RANN UTSAV — annual cultural festival (Nov-Feb), tents at Dhordo. Salt cultivation = livelihood. KUTCH = largest district in India by area.

cards.front:
The KHEJRI tree, sacred + state-tree of Rajasthan, is famous for:

(A) Producing fragrant rose flowers
(B) Drought-tolerant tree (lifeline of Thar)
(C) Bearing apples + temperate fruits
(D) Coniferous needle-leaf evergreen
cards.back:
(B) Drought-tolerant tree (lifeline of Thar)

Physical Features — KHEJRI (Prosopis cineraria) — drought-resistant, very deep roots reaching ground water, leguminous (fixes nitrogen → enriches soil). Multipurpose: fodder (leaves), edible pods (SANGRI — cuisine of Rajasthan), fuelwood. STATE TREE of Rajasthan + Telangana. CULTURAL — sacred to Bishnoi community; CHIPKO origin point in 1730 KHEJARLI MASSACRE — 363 Bishnoi villagers killed by Maharaja's army for protecting khejri trees from being cut for palace construction. Led by Amrita Devi. Considered ONE of EARLIEST environmental movements globally — predates Chipko by 250 years!

cards.front:
The ANDAMAN AND NICOBAR ISLANDS are located in which body of water?

(A) Bay of Bengal (eastern coast of India)
(B) Arabian Sea (western coast) too
(C) Indian Ocean south of mainland.
(D) Lakshadweep Sea (south-west).
cards.back:
(A) Bay of Bengal (eastern coast of India)

Physical Features — ANDAMAN & NICOBAR ISLANDS lie in the BAY OF BENGAL, ~1300 km from the eastern Indian mainland; geographically closer to Myanmar and Indonesia than India. KEY GEOGRAPHY: ~572 islands (only ~38 inhabited); split into ANDAMAN GROUP (north) and NICOBAR GROUP (south), separated by the 10° CHANNEL. CAPITAL: PORT BLAIR (South Andaman). FORMATION: ORIGIN — emerged peaks of a submerged mountain ridge that extends from the Arakan Yoma mountains (Myanmar) to Sumatra (Indonesia). HIGHEST POINT: Saddle Peak (732 m) on North Andaman. ACTIVE VOLCANO: BARREN ISLAND — India's only active volcano, last erupted in 2017. AREA: ~8,249 km²; population ~400,000. STRATEGIC: India's only tri-services COMMAND (Andaman & Nicobar Command, est. 2001) at Port Blair — guards the eastern maritime approaches and the Strait of Malacca chokepoint. INDIGENOUS TRIBES: Jarawa, Sentinelese (uncontacted), Onge, Great Andamanese, Shompen, Nicobarese — protected under Andaman tribal laws. PYQ ANGLE: Andaman/Nicobar features appear in UPSC, SSC, Banking GK 2-3× per year.

cards.front:
LAKSHADWEEP islands are formed primarily by:

(A) Coral atolls and reefs
(B) Volcanic activity (igneous origin)
(C) Tectonic uplift of seabed.
(D) Sediment deposits from rivers.
cards.back:
(A) Coral atolls and reefs

Physical Features — LAKSHADWEEP ('Hundred Thousand Islands' in Sanskrit/Malayalam) is India's smallest UT, located in the ARABIAN SEA, ~200-440 km off Kerala. FORMATION: CORAL ATOLLS — circular reefs around shallow lagoons, built up over millennia by tiny coral polyps depositing calcium carbonate. CONTRAST WITH ANDAMAN: Andaman = mountain peaks (volcanic/tectonic origin); Lakshadweep = coral (biological origin). STATS: 36 islands; only 10 INHABITED; total area ~32 km² (smaller than Connaught Place + a few neighbourhoods!); population ~64,000. CAPITAL: KAVARATTI. LARGEST ISLAND: Andrott (4.84 km²). ENVIRONMENT THREAT: rising sea levels and warming oceans threaten coral bleaching — 2016 mass bleaching killed ~70% of Lakshadweep corals. PEOPLE: ~96% Muslim, Malayalam-speaking; matrilineal customs. ECONOMY: coconut, tuna fishing, tourism (limited entry to preserve ecology). STRATEGIC: India's western maritime border; near international shipping lanes. PYQ FREQUENCY: 'Lakshadweep is coral; Andaman is volcanic' is a high-yield CGL/UPSC fact pair.

cards.front:
BARREN ISLAND, India's only active volcano, is part of which island group?

(A) Andaman group (Bay of Bengal)
(B) Nicobar group (Bay of Bengal)
(C) Lakshadweep (Arabian Sea) alone
(D) Sundarbans (Ganges delta) alone
cards.back:
(A) Andaman group (Bay of Bengal)

Physical Features — BARREN ISLAND (~3 km diameter) lies ~135 km NE of Port Blair in the ANDAMAN group. It's part of a volcanic chain extending from Sumatra to Myanmar. ERUPTIONS: dormant for ~150 years; reactivated 1991 with subsequent eruptions in 1995, 2005, 2017. The 2017 eruption produced ash columns visible from satellite imagery; closely monitored by IIT Hyderabad and ISRO. NARCONDAM ISLAND (also Andaman group) is a DORMANT volcano — last erupted historically thousands of years ago. ECOLOGY: Barren has no human habitation; supports goat and rat populations from prior introductions. NEAREST INHABITED: Port Blair. FORMATION SCIENCE: Barren sits on the boundary where the Indo-Australian plate subducts beneath the Burma plate — same tectonic system that caused the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami. EARTHQUAKE RISK: Andaman region is highly seismic; the 2004 mega-quake (M9.1) caused permanent crustal shifts. EXAM ANGLE: 'Barren Island = only active volcano in India' is a top-10 Indian-geography fact, appears 2-3× per UPSC Prelims cycle. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests precise location + active/dormant distinction.

cards.front:
MAJULI, the world's LARGEST RIVER ISLAND, is situated in:

(A) Brahmaputra River, Assam state
(B) Ganga River, Bihar state alone
(C) Godavari River, Andhra Pradesh
(D) Mahanadi River, Odisha state
cards.back:
(A) Brahmaputra River, Assam state

Physical Features — MAJULI ISLAND lies in the BRAHMAPUTRA river in Assam — until ~2014 it held the Guinness record as the world's largest INHABITED river island; due to severe erosion the title is now contested. AREA: shrunk from ~1250 km² (1950s) to ~880 km² today; loses ~7-8 km² annually to Brahmaputra erosion. POPULATION: ~150,000; predominantly NEO-VAISHNAVITE Assamese culture. RELIGIOUS SIGNIFICANCE: Majuli is the cultural heart of SANKARDEVA's bhakti reform movement (15-16th century); home to ~22 SATTRAS (Vaishnava monastic centres). ADMINISTRATIVE: declared a SEPARATE DISTRICT of Assam in 2016 (India's first river-island district). MIGRATORY BIRDS: thousands of Siberian cranes, pelicans, storks visit annually — Majuli is a bird-lover's destination. THREATS: floods (erosion 50% in 70 years), declining sattra culture, tourism pressure. UNESCO: India bid to add Majuli to World Heritage List in 2004 (still tentative). EXAM ANGLE: 'Majuli + Brahmaputra' is a UPSC, SSC, Assam APSC perennial fact.

cards.front:
Which is the SOUTHERNMOST POINT of the Indian Union?

(A) Indira Point on Great Nicobar Island
(B) Kanyakumari, Tamil Nadu state alone
(C) Point Calimere of Tamil Nadu state
(D) Dhanushkodi of Rameswaram Island
cards.back:
(A) Indira Point on Great Nicobar Island

Physical Features — INDIRA POINT (formerly Pygmalion Point, Parsons Point) on GREAT NICOBAR ISLAND is the southernmost point of the Indian Union at 6°45'10" N latitude. RENAMED in 1985 in honour of Indira Gandhi (Rajiv Gandhi visited that year). KANYAKUMARI is the southernmost point of MAINLAND India (8°4' N) — frequently confused. 2004 TSUNAMI IMPACT: Indira Point's lighthouse was severely damaged; the actual coastline submerged ~4.25 m due to tectonic shift; the island lost ~10 sq km area. CARDINAL POINTS OF INDIA — memorize: NORTHERNMOST: Indira Col, Siachen Glacier (now), or Pulwama district pre-1947 borders. SOUTHERNMOST: Indira Point, Great Nicobar. EASTERNMOST: Kibithu / Walong, Arunachal Pradesh. WESTERNMOST: Sir Creek / Guhar Mota, Gujarat. LATITUDINAL EXTENT: ~30° (8° to 37° N approximately). LONGITUDINAL EXTENT: ~30° (68° to 97° E). PYQ FREQUENCY: cardinal points are top-5 UPSC Prelims geography topics. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests exact territorial boundaries + post-2004 tsunami changes.
cards.option2: Point Calimere of Tamil Nadu state

cards.front:
DIU island is part of which Indian Union Territory?

(A) Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu
(B) Lakshadweep islands group alone
(C) Andaman & Nicobar Islands UT
(D) Puducherry Union Territory alone
cards.back:
(A) Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu

Physical Features — DIU is a small ISLAND off the southern coast of Gujarat (Saurashtra peninsula), connected to mainland by bridges. It's part of the merged UT 'DADRA & NAGAR HAVELI AND DAMAN & DIU' — formed 26 January 2020 when two earlier UTs (DNH and Daman & Diu) were unified. PORTUGUESE HISTORY: Diu was a PORTUGUESE colony from 1535 (treaty with Bahadur Shah of Gujarat) until 1961 (Operation Vijay liberated Goa, Daman, Diu). The Diu fort is a 16th-century Portuguese stronghold — a popular tourist site. UT FORMATION: After Goa became a state in 1987, Daman + Diu remained UTs. Then merged with Dadra & Nagar Haveli in 2020 for administrative efficiency. AREA: Diu ~40 km²; population ~50,000. ECONOMY: tourism, fishing, salt extraction. CULTURE: Portuguese-Catholic heritage (San Sebastian Church) blended with Gujarati culture. PYQ ANGLE: post-2020 UT-merger is a current-affairs fact tested in CGL, RRB, UPSC. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests recent administrative geography changes + colonial-era continuity.

cards.front:
Which island in the Sundarbans is famous as a major HINDU PILGRIMAGE site, especially during Makar Sankranti?

(A) Sagar Island in West Bengal state
(B) Diamond Harbour island alone
(C) Bhitarkanika of Odisha state
(D) Wheeler Island near Odisha coast
cards.back:
(A) Sagar Island in West Bengal state

Physical Features — SAGAR ISLAND (Sagar Dweep) lies at the mouth of the Hooghly (Ganga) river where it meets the Bay of Bengal — South 24 Parganas district, WEST BENGAL. RELIGIOUS SIGNIFICANCE: it hosts the GANGASAGAR MELA every January 14 (Makar Sankranti) — the second-largest annual gathering in India after the Kumbh Mela. ~5 MILLION pilgrims gather to bathe at the Ganga-sea confluence and visit the KAPIL MUNI temple (rebuilt several times due to coastal erosion). MYTHOLOGY: legend says King Sagara's 60,000 sons were burnt to ash by Sage Kapila here; their ashes were liberated to heaven only when Bhagiratha brought the Ganga down (the Ganga-descent narrative). GEOGRAPHY: ~250 km² island, mostly mangrove and farming villages; severely affected by Cyclone Yaas (2021) and rising sea levels (~6 mm/year). RELATED SUNDARBANS: world's largest delta, shared with Bangladesh; UNESCO World Heritage; home to Royal Bengal Tigers. cards.front:
KHYBER PASS (historical entry route into India) lies in:

(B) Sikkim-China border (Nathu La nearby)

HISTORIC INVASION ROUTE into India for ALL major invaders: Aryans, Persians, Greeks (Alexander), Mauryans (other way), Huns, Kushans, Mongols (briefly), Mahmud of Ghazni, Muhammad Ghori, Babur (1526). Other historical Indian PASSES: BOLAN PASS (Pak-Afg, alt route through Balochistan); HINDU KUSH passes (Khyber, Khojak). Within MODERN INDIA: NATHU LA (Sikkim-Tibet), ROHTANG (HP), ZOJI LA (J&K-Ladakh), SHIPKI LA, KARAKORAM PASS. India-China BORDER passes used in historical trade.

ZOJI LA pass connects:

cards.front:
NATHU LA pass on Sikkim-China border was reopened for trade in:

(A) 2006 (after 44 years closed)
(B) 1990 (Cold War end era)
(C) 1947 (Independence year)

cards.back:
(A) 2006 (after 44 years closed)

Physical Features — NATHU LA — pass between SIKKIM (India) + Tibet (China); altitude ~4310 m. CLOSED in 1962 after Sino-Indian war. REOPENED for limited trade in 2006 (after 44 years!). On historic SILK ROUTE branch. Strategic significance: closest land route from India to Lhasa (Tibet); important during 1962 + 1965 wars; 2017 DOKLAM standoff nearby. Nearby: JELEPLA (also pass), GURUDONGMAR LAKE. Other India-China passes (closed for civilian use, often LAC tensions): SHIPKI LA (HP-Tibet), LIPULEKH (Uttarakhand-Tibet), MANA + NITI passes (Uttarakhand). KAILASH-MANSAROVAR YATRA — Indian Hindus go to Mt Kailash via Lipulekh pass (Uttarakhand) or Nathu La. INDIA-CHINA border = LINE OF ACTUAL CONTROL (LAC), 3488 km long, undefined formally.

cards.front:
KARAKORAM PASS (highest pass on India's old SILK ROUTE) is at altitude:

(A) About 5540 m / 18,176 ft
(B) About 3500 m / 11,500 ft (Zoji La)
(C) About 4000 m / 13,000 ft (Nathu La)
(D) About 8000 m / 26,000 ft (Mt Everest)
cards.back:
(A) About 5540 m / 18,176 ft

Physical Features — KARAKORAM PASS — 5540 m, between LADAKH (India) + Xinjiang (China). One of HIGHEST motorable passes — though motorable now in summer with caution; historically only by yak / mule. Once part of SILK ROUTE branch via Yarkand-Leh. Closed since 1949 (China occupation of Tibet/Xinjiang). India SUSPENDED traffic. KHARDUNG LA (Ladakh, 5359 m) — once claimed 'world's highest motorable road' (claim disputed). UMLING LA (recent, 5883 m, also Ladakh) — currently world's HIGHEST motorable road, opened 2017 by BRO. India is MOUNTAINOUS — many high-altitude road records. CHALLENGES: oxygen ~50% of sea level; vehicles labour; engines need carburettor adjustment.

The Himalayas are divided into three main parallel ranges from north to south. Which range is the HIGHEST and contains Mount Everest?

(A) Shivalik (outer)
(B) Middle Himalayas / Himachal / Lesser Himalayas
(C) Greater Himalayas / Himadri / Inner Himalayas
(D) Trans-Himalayas
cards.back:
(C) Greater Himalayas / Himadri / Inner Himalayas

Physical Features — The Himalayas have three longitudinal divisions (from N to S): (1) GREATER HIMALAYAS (Himadri/Inner/Central) — tallest, contains Everest (8,848m), Kanchenjunga (8586m — 3rd highest), Makalu, Cho Oyu, Dhaulagiri; perennial snow; source of major rivers. (2) LESSER HIMALAYAS (Himachal/Middle) — ranges like Pir Panjal, Dhauladhar, Mussoorie, Nag Tibba, Mahabharat; hill stations (Shimla, Mussoorie, Nainital, Darjeeling); avg 3500-5000m. (3) SHIVALIK (Outer/Sub-Himalayas) — 900-1200m, youngest range; covered with dense forests; famous for Siwalik fossils. TRANS-HIMALAYAS (Karakoram, Ladakh, Zaskar) lie NORTH of the Greater Himalayas — K2 (8611m — 2nd highest globally) is in Karakoram.

cards.front:
Which is India's HIGHEST mountain peak (in Indian territory)?

(A) Mount Everest
(B) Kanchenjunga (Sikkim, 8,586 m)
(C) Nanda Devi (Uttarakhand, 7,816 m)
(D) K2 (Karakoram)
cards.back:
(B) Kanchenjunga (Sikkim, 8,586 m)

Physical Features — KANCHENJUNGA (8,586m, Sikkim) is India's highest peak within undisputed Indian territory — also the world's 3rd highest mountain after Everest and K2. MOUNT EVEREST (8848m) is on the Nepal-Tibet (China) border, NOT Indian. K2 (8611m, world's 2nd highest) is in the Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir region (disputed but claimed by both India and Pakistan; practically accessed via Pakistan) — NOT counted as Indian by most authorities. NANDA DEVI (7816m, Uttarakhand) is the 2nd-highest peak within India's actual jurisdiction. Kanchenjunga is sacred to Sikkimese Buddhists — climbers traditionally stop just short of the summit as a mark of respect.

(A) Banihal Pass
(B) Zoji La
(C) Khardung La
(D) Rohtang Pass
cards.back:
(B) Zoji La

Physical Features — ZOJI LA (3528m) in Ladakh connects Srinagar (Kashmir Valley) to Leh via Kargil — the critical road link for Ladakh, closed by snow Dec-May. The Siachen Glacier, known as the world's highest battlefield, is located in which region?

(A) Uttarakhand — Gangotri region
(B) Karakoram Range, Ladakh
(C) Sikkim — Khangchendzonga
(D) Arunachal Pradesh
cards.back:
(B) Karakoram Range, Ladakh

Physical Features — SIACHEN GLACIER (~76 km long, 2nd longest non-polar glacier after Fedchenko in Tajikistan) lies in the Karakoram Range of eastern Ladakh, between the Saltoro Ridge (west) and the main Karakoram (east). India took control of the entire glacier on 13 April 1984 via OPERATION MEGHDOOT (launched by Lt Gen M. L. Chibber + Colonel Narinder 'Bull' Kumar), pre-empting a planned Pakistani occupation. Average altitude ~5400m; temperatures as low as −60°C. The tri-junction of India, Pakistan and China is nearby (Indira Col). Longest glacier system entirely in India: GANGOTRI (30 km, Uttarakhand — source of Bhagirathi-Ganga). India controlled since Operation Meghdoot, 1984.

cards.front:
The Himalayan river system has THREE major rivers originating from Tibet/Himalayas. Which one rises in the TIBETAN PLATEAU and is known there as 'Yarlung Tsangpo'?

(A) Indus
(B) Ganga
(C) Brahmaputra
(D) Yamuna
cards.back:
(C) Brahmaputra

Physical Features — BRAHMAPUTRA rises near Lake Manasarovar (Tibet) as the Yarlung Tsangpo, flows EAST across southern Tibet for ~1700 km, takes a sharp 'Great Bend' around Namcha Barwa, then enters Arunachal Pradesh as the SIANG / DIHANG. Joined by Lohit and Dibang at Sadiya → becomes the BRAHMAPUTRA flowing west through Assam. Enters Bangladesh as JAMUNA, merges with Padma (Ganga) and Meghna before emptying into the Bay of Bengal. INDUS also rises near Manasarovar, flows NW into Ladakh and then PoK. GANGA rises as Bhagirathi from Gangotri Glacier (UK), joined by Alaknanda at Devprayag to officially become the Ganga. Yamuna rises at Yamunotri (UK).

cards.front:
A tropical cyclone forms over the Bay of Bengal and moves toward the Odisha coast. Which of the following factors does NOT contribute to its intensification?

(B) Presence of the Coriolis force at sufficient latitude (> ~5° N)

cards.back:

Physical Features — HIGH vertical wind shear DISRUPTS cyclone structure and INHIBITS intensification. Low shear is what a cyclone needs. cards.front:
The 'RING OF FIRE' refers to a horseshoe-shaped zone of frequent volcanic + earthquake activity around the:

(A) Atlantic Ocean rim, including Iceland and Brazil
(B) Pacific Ocean rim, including Japan, Indonesia, Andes
(C) Indian Ocean rim, including Madagascar and India
(D) Arctic Ocean rim around the North Pole basin
cards.back:
(B) Pacific Ocean rim, including Japan, Indonesia, Andes

Physical Features — RING OF FIRE — ~40,000 km horseshoe around the Pacific Ocean. Hosts ~75% of world's active + dormant volcanoes and ~90% of earthquakes. Caused by SUBDUCTION at convergent plate boundaries — denser oceanic plates dive beneath continental plates → magma + earthquakes. Includes: Andes (S America), Cascades (US), Aleutian arc, Kamchatka, Japan, Philippines, Indonesia, NZ. Mt Fuji, Krakatoa, Vesuvius (no — Mediterranean), Mt St Helens, Pinatubo all here. Indian Ocean has fewer such margins (mostly mid-ocean spreading + the Sunda subduction zone in the east — where 2004 tsunami quake occurred).

cards.option2: Indian Ocean rim, including Madagascar and India

(B) Magnitude (energy released) on a logarithmic scale

Physical Features — Richter scale — measures MAGNITUDE (energy released at the source). LOGARITHMIC: each whole number is 10× the amplitude and ~32× the energy. Magnitude 7 quake releases ~32× more energy than magnitude 6. Devised by Charles Richter (1935) for southern California. Modern seismologists use the MOMENT MAGNITUDE SCALE (M_w) for large quakes (Richter saturates above ~7). MERCALLI scale (Distractor 1) — measures intensity / observed effects (1-12 Roman numerals); subjective. Distractors 3, 4 are different parameters.

cards.front:
The point INSIDE the earth where an earthquake originates is called the:

(A) Epicentre, the location directly above the source
(B) Focus or hypocentre, the actual subterranean origin
(C) Magnitude reading observed on the recorder
(D) Tsunami zone of inundation along coasts
cards.back:
(B) Focus or hypocentre, the actual subterranean origin

Physical Features — FOCUS / HYPOCENTRE — the actual underground point of energy release. EPICENTRE — point on Earth's surface directly ABOVE the focus (where shaking is usually most intense). Quake depth classification: SHALLOW (< 70 km) — most damaging, most common; INTERMEDIATE (70-300 km); DEEP (> 300 km) — usually felt little at surface, occur in subduction zones. Distractor 1 wrongly defines focus as epicentre. Distractors 3, 4 are unrelated terms.

cards.front:
The INDIA's only ACTIVE volcano is:

(A) Mt Abu in Rajasthan, of the Aravalli range
(B) Barren Island in the Andaman Sea, off mainland
(C) Mt Girnar in Gujarat, of religious significance
(D) Mt Mahendragiri of Tamil Nadu hill ranges
cards.back:
(B) Barren Island in the Andaman Sea, off mainland

Physical Features — BARREN ISLAND — in the Andaman Sea, ~135 km NE of Port Blair. Only active volcano in India. Stratovolcano on the Burma microplate at the Sunda subduction. Erupted multiple times — most recently 2017, 2018, 2022 (small). NARCONDAM ISLAND nearby — DORMANT volcano. Mt Abu (Rajasthan) — Aravalli highland, NOT volcanic. Mt Girnar (Gujarat) — Junagadh, granitic intrusion (~250 Ma old), highly eroded, sacred but not active. Distractor 4 — Tamil Nadu mountains aren't volcanic.

cards.front:
Earthquakes are caused primarily by:

(A) The rotation of the Earth speeding up over time
(B) Sudden release of stored elastic energy along faults
(C) The Moon's gravitational pull as the tides change
(D) Atmospheric pressure changes during major storms
cards.back:
(B) Sudden release of stored elastic energy along faults

Physical Features — Plate tectonics — plates move slowly (~few cm/yr); friction at boundaries means stress builds up over decades-centuries. When stress exceeds rock strength → SUDDEN slip along a FAULT line → earthquake. Energy radiated as SEISMIC WAVES (P-waves: primary, faster, longitudinal; S-waves: secondary, slower, transverse; Surface waves — most damaging). Most quakes occur at plate boundaries (transform — San Andreas, convergent — Himalayas, divergent — mid-Atlantic ridge). Distractor 3 — tidal forces affect Earth but don't drive quakes. Distractor 4 — atmospheric effects negligible.

cards.front:
VOLCANIC ERUPTIONS contribute to soil fertility because:

(A) Lava cools to form solid bedrock that nourishes plants
(B) Volcanic ash + lava weather to release minerals beneficial to soil
(C) Volcanic gases like SO₂ are good plant fertilisers
(D) Heat from eruptions sterilises the soil for new growth
cards.back:
(B) Volcanic ash + lava weather to release minerals beneficial to soil

Physical Features — Volcanic ash + weathered lava (basalt) release minerals (Ca, Mg, K, P, micronutrients) → among the most fertile soils on Earth. Examples: Java (Indonesia) — densely populated and farmed despite frequent eruptions; Italy — Campania near Vesuvius famed for tomato + lemon production; Mt Etna's slopes — vineyards, citrus. India: Deccan basalt soils give rise to BLACK COTTON SOIL (regur) — high water-holding capacity, famous for cotton cultivation. Distractor 1 — fresh bedrock isn't fertile until weathered. Distractor 3 — SO₂ is harmful, not a fertiliser. Distractor 4 — sterilisation is harmful, not beneficial.

cards.front:
The 2004 BOXING DAY TSUNAMI was triggered by an earthquake near the coast of:

(A) Japan, the Tohoku coast in the Pacific Ocean
(B) Sumatra in Indonesia, in the Indian Ocean
(C) California coast along the San Andreas fault
(D) Chile coast in the Pacific Ring of Fire
cards.back:
(B) Sumatra in Indonesia, in the Indian Ocean

Physical Features — 26 December 2004 — Mw 9.1-9.3 megathrust earthquake near SUMATRA, Indonesia (Indian Ocean). 3rd largest ever recorded. Triggered tsunami waves up to 30 m → killed ~230,000 across 14 countries (Indonesia worst — Aceh; then Sri Lanka, India — TN coast, Andaman/Nicobar, Thailand, Maldives, even African coasts). India set up Indian Ocean Tsunami Warning System after this disaster (operational since 2007, INCOIS Hyderabad). 2011 TŌHOKU earthquake (Japan, Mw 9.1) caused Fukushima nuclear disaster. 1960 Valdivia (Chile, Mw 9.5) — largest ever recorded.

cards.front:
GANGOTRI Glacier is the SOURCE of which major river?

(A) Bhagirathi (origin of the Ganges)
(B) Yamuna originates at Yamunotri
(C) Brahmaputra (Tibet origin only)
(D) Sutlej (Tibetan origin again)
cards.back:
(A) Bhagirathi (origin of the Ganges)

Rivers & Water Bodies — GANGOTRI GLACIER — one of the LARGEST glaciers in the Indian Himalaya (~30 km long, ~2-4 km wide, area ~143 sq km). Located in UTTARKASHI district of UTTARAKHAND, at altitude 4,000-7,000 m. SOURCE OF: BHAGIRATHI river — which joins the ALAKNANDA at DEVPRAYAG to form the GANGES (Ganga). The snout of Gangotri Glacier is called GAUMUKH ('cow's mouth' — the glacier's icy mouth resembles a cow). PILGRIMAGE: Gomukh is sacred — annual yatra. RETREAT: Gangotri has been retreating ~22 m/year on average over recent decades — mostly due to climate change. MAJOR RIVERS and their HIMALAYAN GLACIER ORIGINS: (1) BHAGIRATHI/GANGA → Gangotri Glacier. (2) ALAKNANDA → Satopanth + Bhagirath Kharak Glaciers (Garhwal). (3) YAMUNA → Yamunotri Glacier (also called Champasar Glacier). (4) MANDAKINI → Chorabari Glacier (Kedarnath). (5) GANDAK → Nepalese Himalayan glaciers. (6) KOSI → Khumbu region glaciers (Nepal). (7) BRAHMAPUTRA → Chemayungdung Glacier (Tibet, near Kailash). (8) INDUS → Sengge Khabab Glacier (near Kailash, Tibet). (9) SUTLEJ → Lake Rakshastal/Mansarovar (Tibet). PYQ FREQUENCY: river-glacier pairings appear in SSC, UPSC, NDA 1-2× per cycle.

cards.front:
SIACHEN GLACIER, the world's highest battlefield, is located in:

(A) Eastern Karakoram (Ladakh)
(B) Western Himalayas of HP only
(C) Central Nepal Himalayas now
(D) Eastern Himalayas of Sikkim
cards.back:
(A) Eastern Karakoram (Ladakh)

Rivers & Water Bodies — SIACHEN GLACIER — located in the EASTERN KARAKORAM range (NOT Himalaya proper) in LADAKH, India. Length ~76 km — the LONGEST glacier in the NON-POLAR REGIONS. Altitude 5,400-6,000 m at the snout; surrounding peaks 7,000+ m. NAME: 'Siachen' = 'place of the wild rose' in Balti language. STRATEGIC IMPORTANCE: WORLD'S HIGHEST BATTLEFIELD — Indian Army deployment since OPERATION MEGHDOOT (April 1984), under General K. Sundarji's plan. India holds the entire glacier and the SALTORO RIDGE west of it; Pakistan holds positions on the lower western slopes. CONFLICT: Siachen War — over 1000 deaths each side, mostly from WEATHER (frostbite, avalanches, altitude sickness — NOT combat). LIFE AT POSTS: temperatures down to −60°C; soldiers serve 90-day rotations. INDUS DRAINAGE: Siachen feeds the NUBRA RIVER → SHYOK RIVER → INDUS. STRATEGIC: dominates routes from Pakistan-occupied Kashmir to Aksai Chin (China). RECENT: 2016 avalanche killed 10 Indian soldiers at Sonam post — Lance Naik HANUMANTHAPPA was found alive after 6 days, died in hospital. ENVIRONMENTAL: glacier retreating ~5-8 m/year; concerns over military pollution. PYQ FREQUENCY: Siachen geography in UPSC, SSC, defence exams.

cards.front:
Which glacier is the source of the YAMUNA river?

(A) Yamunotri Glacier (Champasar)
(B) Gangotri Glacier feeds Ganga
(C) Pindari Glacier of Kumaon area
(D) Zemu Glacier of Sikkim alone
cards.back:
(A) Yamunotri Glacier (Champasar)

Rivers & Water Bodies — YAMUNOTRI GLACIER — also known as CHAMPASAR GLACIER — source of the YAMUNA river. Located in UTTARKASHI district, UTTARAKHAND, at ~6,387 m altitude on the slopes of BANDARPUNCH peak. The actual source point is a SACRED hot spring at YAMUNOTRI temple (3,293 m altitude); the temple is one of the CHAR DHAM sites (along with Gangotri, Kedarnath, Badrinath). YAMUNA river: longest tributary of the Ganga (1,376 km). Joins Ganga at TRIVENI SANGAM, ALLAHABAD (Prayagraj) — the holy confluence. KEY YAMUNA TRIBUTARIES: Tons (largest), Hindon, Chambal, Betwa, Ken, Sind. KUMBH MELA: Allahabad's Maha Kumbh (every 12 years; Ardh Kumbh every 6) draws ~10+ crore pilgrims — one of the largest peaceful gatherings in human history. POLLUTION: Yamuna heavily polluted in Delhi stretch — efforts under National River Conservation Plan, Yamuna Action Plan. CHAR DHAM YATRA glaciers all-in-Garhwal: Yamunotri (Yamuna), Gangotri (Bhagirathi-Ganga), Kedarnath (Mandakini, Chorabari Glacier), Badrinath (Alaknanda, Satopanth Glacier). PYQ FREQUENCY: Char Dham + glacier links are top SSC, UPSC, NCERT geography MCQs.

cards.front:
ZEMU Glacier, the largest glacier of the eastern Himalaya, lies in which Indian state?

(A) Sikkim (eastern Himalayas state)
(B) Arunachal Pradesh easternmost state
(C) Uttarakhand of central Himalaya
(D) Himachal Pradesh western Himalayas
cards.back:
(A) Sikkim (eastern Himalayas state)

Rivers & Water Bodies — ZEMU GLACIER — largest glacier in the EASTERN HIMALAYAS, located in NORTH SIKKIM, on the eastern flank of KANGCHENJUNGA (the world's THIRD HIGHEST mountain at 8,586 m). Length: ~26 km. Altitude: ~4,000-7,000 m. SOURCE of the TEESTA RIVER (via the Zemu Chhu, which feeds the Lachen Chhu, then Teesta). KANGCHENJUNGA — five peaks (Sanskrit Kanchanjangha = 'five treasures of snow'); shared by Sikkim (India) and Nepal. First climbed: 1955 (British expedition led by Charles Evans; out of respect for Sikkimese beliefs, climbers stopped a few feet below summit — tradition continues). TEESTA RIVER: flows south through Sikkim and West Bengal; joins BRAHMAPUTRA in Bangladesh. Major hydropower potential — multiple ongoing projects. RECENT — OCT 2023: TEESTA-3 dam burst from a GLACIAL LAKE OUTBURST FLOOD (GLOF) — South Lhonak Lake glacier-lake breach killed 100+ in flash floods. Major reminder of climate-change risks. OTHER EASTERN HIMALAYA GLACIERS: Kanchenjunga's other glaciers (Talung, Yalung), Bhutanese glaciers (drain into Brahmaputra). PYQ FREQUENCY: state-glacier pairings in NCERT-driven SSC, NDA 1× per cycle.

cards.front:
PINDARI Glacier, a popular trekking destination, is located in:

(A) Kumaon Himalaya (Uttarakhand)
(B) Garhwal Himalaya (Uttarakhand)
(C) Spiti Valley region (Himachal)
(D) Kashmir Valley (Jammu region)
cards.back:
(A) Kumaon Himalaya (Uttarakhand)

Rivers & Water Bodies — PINDARI GLACIER — located in the KUMAON HIMALAYA, BAGESHWAR district of UTTARAKHAND. ~3 km long, altitude 3,353 m at zero-point (the trek's endpoint). Source of PINDAR RIVER, which flows into the ALAKNANDA at KARNAPRAYAG. POPULAR TREK: 'Pindari Glacier Trek' — gentle, moderate; reachable in ~5-6 days from base at Bharari/Loharkhet. Since 2013 floods, accessibility has been disrupted in places. KUMAON vs GARHWAL: both regions in Uttarakhand. KUMAON = eastern half (Almora, Bageshwar, Pithoragarh, Nainital, Champawat, Udham Singh Nagar). GARHWAL = western half (Chamoli, Tehri Garhwal, Pauri, Rudraprayag, Uttarkashi, Dehradun, Haridwar). NEAR PINDARI: KAFNI Glacier (close trek), MILAM Glacier (longer, NEAR INDO-NEPAL-TIBET TRIJUNCTION) — Milam is the largest Kumaon glacier (~16 km long). NANDA DEVI (7,816 m): India's 2nd highest peak, in Chamoli; surrounded by Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve (UNESCO Heritage). NOTABLE TREKS in UTTARAKHAND: Valley of Flowers (Bhyundar), Kedarkantha, Roopkund (skeleton lake), Hemkund Sahib. PYQ ANGLE: Kumaon-Garhwal distinctions and glacier-trek locations in SSC, NDA, state PSC.

cards.front:
Which scientific organisation studies Himalayan glaciers and the cryosphere in India?

(A) Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology
(B) Geological Survey of India primarily
(C) National Atlas (NATMO) for maps
(D) Indian Council of Agricultural Research
cards.back:
(A) Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology

Rivers & Water Bodies — WADIA INSTITUTE OF HIMALAYAN GEOLOGY (WIHG) — autonomous research institute under the Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India. Established 1968 in DEHRADUN, Uttarakhand. Named after D.N. WADIA, a pioneer Indian geologist. PRIMARY FOCUS: geological studies of the Himalayan and adjoining regions — glaciology, seismology, tectonics, hydrology, paleobiology. KEY OUTPUTS: glacial mass-balance studies, retreat-rate measurements (e.g., Gangotri Glacier monitoring since 1990s). Documented that ~75% of Himalayan glaciers are RETREATING. RELATED ORGANIZATIONS: (1) NATIONAL CENTRE FOR POLAR AND OCEAN RESEARCH (NCPOR), Goa — runs Himadri (Arctic), Bharati & Maitri (Antarctic) stations; cryosphere research. (2) GEOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA (GSI), Kolkata — broader geological mapping. (3) NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF DISASTER MANAGEMENT (NIDM) — risks from glaciers (GLOFs, avalanches). (4) ICIMOD (International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development), Kathmandu — Hindu Kush Himalaya Monitoring & Assessment Programme (HIMAP). CLIMATE CHANGE IMPACT: 2019 ICIMOD report — Himalayas could lose 1/3 of glaciers by 2100 even if 1.5°C warming target met. PYQ ANGLE: research-organization MCQs in UPSC PT, SSC GA.

cards.front:
A GLACIAL LAKE OUTBURST FLOOD (GLOF) is a sudden release of water from:

(A) A glacier-fed lake breaching its dam
(B) A river dam reservoir gates opening
(C) Underground aquifer breaks the surface
(D) Heavy monsoon rains in the basin
cards.back:
(A) A glacier-fed lake breaching its dam

Rivers & Water Bodies — GLOF = GLACIAL LAKE OUTBURST FLOOD — a sudden, catastrophic release of water from a glacier-dammed or moraine-dammed lake when its natural barrier breaks. CAUSE: glacial retreat creates LAKES at the snout (or in moraines) — held back by ice/loose-rock dams; breach is triggered by avalanche, earthquake, or simply gradual erosion. INDIAN HIMALAYA — recent MAJOR GLOFs: (1) UTTARAKHAND FLOODS, JUNE 2013 — Kedarnath disaster — 5,000+ deaths; Chorabari Lake outburst combined with cloudburst. (2) CHAMOLI, FEB 2021 — Rishi Ganga + Dhauliganga flash flood; killed 200+; ice-rock avalanche from a hanging glacier. (3) SIKKIM, OCT 2023 — South Lhonak Lake GLOF — killed 100+, destroyed Teesta-3 hydropower dam, displaced 25,000+. RISK ASSESSMENT: ~7,500+ glacial lakes in the Hindu Kush Himalaya region; ~25-30 are 'high-risk' GLOF candidates. WARNING SYSTEMS: India deploys SATELLITE MONITORING (ISRO), early-warning sensors at vulnerable lakes; ICIMOD does regional coordination. CLIMATE CHANGE LINK: warmer temperatures → faster glacier melt → larger and more numerous lakes → higher GLOF risk. PYQ ANGLE: GLOFs are rising in importance — UPSC PT/Mains/Geography optional 1× per cycle. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests climate-disaster knowledge.

cards.front:
The INDUS river originates near Lake MANASAROVAR in:

(A) Sikkim, in eastern Himalayas only
(B) Tibet (China), Kailash range region
(C) Uttarakhand, central Himalayan region
(D) Pakistan-occupied Kashmir mountains
cards.back:
(B) Tibet (China), Kailash range region

Rivers & Water Bodies — Indus rises in TIBET near Mt. KAILASH and Lake Mansarovar (Singi Khabab — 'Lion Mouth' spring). Flows NW through Ladakh, Pakistan, Arabian Sea (Karachi). Total length ~3180 km. Right-bank tributaries (less): Kabul. Left-bank (more): JHELUM, CHENAB, RAVI, BEAS, SUTLEJ — the 'PANJ' (5 rivers) of Punjab. Indus Water Treaty (1960) — eastern (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) to India; western (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) to Pakistan. Mansarovar is also source of: Sutlej, Brahmaputra, Karnali (Ghaghara).

cards.front:
The GANGA originates from the GANGOTRI glacier (as Bhagirathi). It officially becomes 'Ganga' after merging with Alaknanda at:

(A) Rudraprayag, where Mandakini joins
(B) Devprayag in Uttarakhand state
(C) Rishikesh, the holy yoga town
(D) Haridwar, where it leaves the hills
cards.back:
(B) Devprayag in Uttarakhand state

Rivers & Water Bodies — DEVPRAYAG = confluence of BHAGIRATHI (from Gangotri, Gaumukh) + ALAKNANDA (from Satopanth, Bhagirath Kharak glaciers). Below Devprayag → river is officially called GANGA. Five PRAYAGS (Panch Prayag) of Uttarakhand, in upstream order on Alaknanda: VISHNUPRAYAG (with Dhauliganga) → NANDPRAYAG (with Nandakini) → KARNAPRAYAG (with Pindar) → RUDRAPRAYAG (with Mandakini, from Kedarnath) → DEVPRAYAG (with Bhagirathi). Ganga then enters plains at HARIDWAR.

The BRAHMAPUTRA enters India from China at the border of:

(A) Sikkim, in extreme north-eastern hills
(B) Arunachal Pradesh as Siang/Dihang
(C) West Bengal, near the Sundarbans
(D) Nagaland, the Naga eastern hills
cards.back:
(B) Arunachal Pradesh as Siang/Dihang

Rivers & Water Bodies — Brahmaputra (Sanskrit = 'son of Brahma'): in Tibet — TSANGPO (~1700 km along east-west valley north of Himalayas); enters India through ARUNACHAL PRADESH as SIANG / DIHANG (after the great U-bend, Tsangpo gorge — world's deepest). cards.front:
Which is the LARGEST tributary of the GANGA, sometimes called the GANGA OF BIHAR?

(A) Kosi, the 'Sorrow of Bihar'
(B) Yamuna, longest tributary of Ganga
(C) Ghaghara, joins near Chhapra Bihar
(D) Son, the largest right-bank tributary
cards.back:
(B) Yamuna, longest tributary of Ganga

Rivers & Water Bodies — YAMUNA — longest + largest tributary of Ganga (~1376 km). Source: Yamunotri glacier. Joins Ganga at PRAYAGRAJ (Allahabad) — TRIVENI SANGAM (with mythical Saraswati). Yamuna's own tributaries: Chambal, Sind, Betwa, Ken (peninsular rivers). Other Ganga tributaries from Himalayas (left bank): Ramganga, GHAGHARA, GANDAK, KOSI. Right bank: Yamuna, SON, Chambal-via-Yamuna. KOSI = 'Sorrow of Bihar' (frequent flooding, channel-shifting). 'Ganga of Bihar' = Ganga itself; 'Yamuna' was meant as longest tributary.

cards.front:
Himalayan rivers are PERENNIAL (flow year-round) because:

(A) They flow through deep canyons always
(B) Fed by glacier melt + monsoon rains
(C) They start from underground springs
(D) Their basins receive heavy snow only
cards.back:
(B) Fed by glacier melt + monsoon rains

Rivers & Water Bodies — Himalayan rivers — PERENNIAL (year-round flow) because of TWO sources: (1) GLACIER + SNOWMELT in summer (when monsoon hasn't started — keeps rivers flowing in pre-monsoon months); (2) MONSOON RAINS in summer + autumn. Peninsular rivers (Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Cauvery) are mostly RAIN-FED → reduce dramatically in dry season; some smaller streams dry up. Glacier-fed perennial flow is critical for irrigation, drinking water, hydropower in north India. Climate change (faster glacier retreat) → first MORE flow, then less — major future concern.

Devastating floods in Bihar's North plains (most famous — 2008 Kosi flood, 3M displaced after embankment breach). Distractor 1 — Damodar = 'Sorrow of Bengal' (now tamed by DVC dams). The Bhakra-Nangal Dam, India's first major multipurpose project after Independence, is built on the:

(A) Beas
(B) Sutlej (between Himachal Pradesh and Punjab)
(C) Yamuna
(D) Ravi
cards.back:
(B) Sutlej (between Himachal Pradesh and Punjab)

Rivers & Water Bodies — Bhakra-Nangal — Sutlej. Bhakra Dam: 226 m high (one of the tallest gravity dams in the world); Govind Sagar reservoir behind it (named after Sikh guru Gobind Singh). Nangal Dam — downstream of Bhakra, smaller, regulates flow. Inaugurated 1963 by Pt Nehru — called it a 'temple of modern India'. Benefits Punjab + Haryana + Rajasthan + HP (irrigation + hydropower). Capacity: 1,325 MW. Managed by BBMB (Bhakra-Beas Management Board). Beas — Pong Dam (HP). Yamuna — Tehri (no, Tehri is on Bhagirathi); on Yamuna there's Hathnikund Barrage. Ravi — Thein/Ranjit Sagar Dam.

(A) Alaknanda
(B) Bhagirathi (a head-stream of the Ganga, in Uttarakhand)
(C) Yamuna

cards.back:

Rivers & Water Bodies — Tehri Dam — Bhagirathi River, Uttarakhand. Height 260.5 m (TALLEST dam in India; among the top 10 highest in the world). Earth + rock-fill type. The Bhagirathi merges with the Alaknanda at Devprayag to form the Ganga. cards.back:
(B) Krishna (in Andhra Pradesh-Telangana border, Nalgonda + Guntur districts)

Named after Nagarjuna, the 2nd-century Buddhist scholar; the nearby site Nagarjunakonda is an important Buddhist archaeological site (now an island in the reservoir; relics relocated). Generates 815 MW + irrigates ~10 lakh hectares. Krishna's other major projects: Srisailam (upstream of Nagarjuna Sagar), Almatti, Tungabhadra (on tributary). Cauvery — Mettur Dam, Krishna Raja Sagara (KRS).

cards.front:
WULAR LAKE, the largest freshwater lake in India, is in which region?

(A) Jammu and Kashmir (Kashmir Valley)
(B) Uttarakhand (further south now)
(C) Sikkim (eastern Himalaya area)
(D) Himachal Pradesh (further west)
cards.back:
(A) Jammu and Kashmir (Kashmir Valley)

Rivers & Water Bodies — WULAR LAKE — INDIA'S LARGEST FRESHWATER LAKE; located in BANDIPORA district, KASHMIR VALLEY (J&K). Area: ~30-260 sq km (varies seasonally — monsoons swell it). Source: JHELUM RIVER flows through it; major regulator of Jhelum's flow. KEY FEATURES: high biodiversity — fish (carp, schizothorax), waterfowl (migratory birds in winter), aquatic plants (lotus, water chestnut). Locally important: ~50,000 people depend on Wular for fishing, boating, water-chestnut harvesting. CONSERVATION: RAMSAR site since 1990; threatened by encroachment, pollution, willow plantation (introduced by British, choked native vegetation). RAMSAR CONVENTION: 1971 international treaty for wetland conservation; INDIA has 80+ Ramsar sites (2024). KEY INDIAN LAKES (memorize): (1) WULAR — J&K (largest fresh). (2) DAL LAKE — Srinagar (famous houseboats, shikara rides). (3) PANGONG TSO — Ladakh (saltwater, China border). (4) TSOMORIRI — Ladakh (saltwater high altitude). (5) NAINITAL — Uttarakhand. (6) BHIMTAL, NAUKUCHIATAL — Uttarakhand. (7) CHILIKA — Odisha (largest brackish, INDIA's largest lake by area). (8) PULICAT — TN/AP (2nd largest brackish). (9) VEMBANAD — Kerala (longest, 96 km). cards.front:
CHILIKA LAKE, the largest BRACKISH-water lake in INDIA, is in which state?

(A) Odisha (eastern coast, Bay of Bengal)
(B) Andhra Pradesh (Pulicat-area)
(C) Tamil Nadu (eastern coast also)
(D) West Bengal (Sundarbans area)
cards.back:
(A) Odisha (eastern coast, Bay of Bengal)

Rivers & Water Bodies — CHILIKA LAKE — INDIA'S LARGEST coastal LAGOON / BRACKISH-water lake; located in ODISHA (Puri, Khurda, Ganjam districts), connected to BAY OF BENGAL by a narrow channel. Area: ~1,100 sq km (avg); summer ~1,100 sq km, monsoon ~1,165 sq km. ECOSYSTEM: BRACKISH (mix of fresh river water + sea water); supports unique biodiversity. SIGNIFICANCE: (1) RAMSAR SITE (1981) — INDIA'S FIRST Ramsar wetland. (2) HOSTS ~1 MILLION migratory birds in winter from Central Asia, Mongolia, Siberia (largest wintering grounds for migratory water birds in India). Birds include flamingos, cranes, herons, ducks, sandpipers. (3) IRRAWADDY DOLPHIN — endangered species; ~150-200 in Chilika (one of largest populations). (4) FISHING industry: ~150,000 fishermen depend on it; produces ~13,000 tonnes/year. (5) Biodiversity: ~700 species of plants/animals. INSTITUTIONS: Chilika Development Authority (CDA, 1992) — manages conservation. PROBLEMS: SILTATION, decreased connection to sea, eutrophication. RECENT: in 2000, a NEW MOUTH was opened into the sea — improved salinity, fish stocks, ecology. INDIA'S LARGEST LAKE BY AREA: CHILIKA (1,100+ sq km) — beats freshwater Wular. WULAR LAKE is largest FRESHWATER lake; Chilika is largest BRACKISH and largest by total area. PYQ FREQUENCY: Chilika in UPSC, SSC, NDA 1-2× per cycle.

cards.front:
LOKTAK LAKE, famous for unique floating PHUMDIS (vegetation islands), is in:

(A) Manipur (the only floating-island lake)
(B) Mizoram (a different NE state)
(C) Assam (Brahmaputra valley area)
(D) Nagaland (Indo-Myanmar area)
cards.back:
(A) Manipur (the only floating-island lake)

Rivers & Water Bodies — LOKTAK LAKE — MANIPUR's largest natural lake (~287 sq km); unique for its FLOATING ISLANDS called PHUMDIS — heterogeneous mass of vegetation, soil, organic matter that floats on water surface; some big enough to support people. WORLD'S ONLY FLOATING NATIONAL PARK: KEIBUL LAMJAO NATIONAL PARK on the southern part of Loktak — protects the SANGAI (brow-antlered deer, Cervus eldii eldii) — Manipur's STATE ANIMAL; critically endangered (~250 left as of 2024). RAMSAR SITE since 1990. ECOLOGY: phumdis SUSTAIN about 200 species of aquatic plants, ~100 species of birds, ~400 species of animals. SOURCE: drained by KHUGA, NAMBUL, and other rivers; outlet is MANIPUR RIVER. CONCERNS: shrinking lake area, pollution from Imphal (state capital, ~50 km away), invasive water hyacinth, sedimentation. ITHAI BARRAGE (1983) — built for hydropower (LOKTAK PROJECT, 105 MW); altered water levels, contributing to ecological problems. CULTURAL: Loktak is central to Manipuri culture; festivals, songs, traditional fishing methods. NEAR ATTRACTIONS: KANGLA Fort (Imphal), Imphal War Cemetery, KEIBUL LAMJAO. NORTH-EAST INDIA OVERVIEW: 7 sister states (Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura) + Sikkim. PYQ FREQUENCY: Loktak-Manipur in UPSC, SSC, NDA 1× per cycle.

cards.front:
VEMBANAD LAKE, INDIA's longest lake (96 km), is in:

(A) Kerala (backwaters of Alleppey)
(B) Tamil Nadu (Coromandel coast)
(C) Karnataka (Mangalore coast)
(D) Goa (only Mandovi estuary)
cards.back:
(A) Kerala (backwaters of Alleppey)

Rivers & Water Bodies — VEMBANAD LAKE — INDIA's LONGEST lake (~96 km); area ~2,033 sq km when including all backwaters; located in KERALA (Alappuzha, Ernakulam, Kottayam districts). PART of the famous KERALA BACKWATERS — interconnected lagoons, channels, lakes. NAMED differently in different stretches: 'Vembanad' (Kottayam region), 'Punnamada Lake' (Alappuzha), 'Kochi Lake' (Ernakulam, near Kochi). UNESCO WORLD HERITAGE — backwaters not, but a Ramsar site since 2002. TOURISM: HOUSEBOATS ('kettuvallam' — 'kettu' = tied, 'vallam' = boat) — converted from cargo boats; iconic backwater experience; ~2-day cruises popular with foreign + domestic tourists. NEHRU TROPHY BOAT RACE held annually on Punnamada Lake (Alappuzha) — 100+ row boats compete; massive cultural event since 1952; 2024 winner: NADUBHAGOM CHUNDAN. ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES: pollution (industrial + sewage from Kochi), encroachment, reduced freshwater flow due to Thanneermukkom barrier. KEY: Thanneermukkom Salt Water Barrier (1976) — reduced salinity inflow but altered ecology. ECONOMIC: rice farming on POLDERS (reclaimed wetlands), fishing, prawns, mussels, coir industry, tourism. KERALA-WATERWAY-FACTS: 41 west-flowing rivers in Kerala drain into Arabian Sea via these backwaters. PYQ FREQUENCY: Vembanad-Kerala in SSC, UPSC GA 1× per cycle.

cards.front:
SAMBHAR LAKE, the largest INLAND SALT lake of INDIA, is in:

(A) Rajasthan (near Jaipur city)
(B) Gujarat (Rann of Kutch area)
(C) Maharashtra (Lonar lake area)
(D) Andhra Pradesh (Pulicat near)
cards.back:
(A) Rajasthan (near Jaipur city)

Rivers & Water Bodies — SAMBHAR SALT LAKE — INDIA's LARGEST INLAND SALT LAKE; located in JAIPUR & NAGAUR districts of RAJASTHAN, ~80 km W of Jaipur. Area: ~190-230 sq km (varies seasonally). HISTORICAL: source of SALT for centuries — mentioned in Mahabharata, given as DOWRY at Maratha-Rajput marriage 1730 between Marwar (Rajasthan) and Maratha empire. SALT PRODUCTION: ~9% of India's total salt comes from Sambhar (~200,000 tonnes/year); via solar evaporation. UNIQUE FEATURE: ~3 m DEEPER salt content than ocean; salinity 7-8% (vs ocean 3.5%). HABITAT: Greater FLAMINGOS gather here in thousands during monsoon — beautiful pink-water spectacle (water turns pink from algae blooms in salt-rich conditions). Other migratory birds: pelicans, cranes, ducks. RAMSAR SITE since 1990. AREA: average 19 km × 4 km, irregular shape. RECENT (2019): mass bird-die-off (~25,000+ birds) due to AVIAN BOTULISM linked to climate change (longer-stagnant water). RECOVERY ongoing. RAJASTHAN's WATER BODIES: SAMBHAR, PUSHKAR (sacred lake, Pushkar town), JAISAMAND (Udaipur, largest artificial lake), PICHOLA + FATEH SAGAR (Udaipur), ANA SAGAR (Ajmer). RAJASTHAN largest state by area; semi-arid; lakes are critical for water + ecology. PYQ FREQUENCY: Sambhar-salt-Rajasthan in SSC, UPSC, NDA 1-2× per cycle.

cards.front:
PANGONG TSO LAKE, situated at high altitude in Ladakh, has its border with which country?

(A) China (~60% of lake in Tibet)
(B) Pakistan (Kashmir Northern area)
(C) Nepal (further south now)
(D) Bhutan (southeastern Himalaya)
cards.back:
(A) China (~60% of lake in Tibet)

Rivers & Water Bodies — PANGONG TSO ('PANGONG LAKE' in Tibetan; 'tso' = lake) — high-altitude (~4,250 m / 13,900 ft) endorheic (no outflow) saline lake in EASTERN LADAKH. ~134 km long, ~5 km wide; ~700 sq km total area. SHARED: ~40% in INDIA (Ladakh, Indo-Tibetan border) + ~60% in CHINA (Tibet Autonomous Region) — runs ALONG THE LAC (Line of Actual Control). LAC: India-China de facto border (not formally agreed); origin of multiple military standoffs. CONFLICT: 2020 LADAKH STANDOFF — major Indo-China tensions; included clashes at Pangong Tso's NORTH BANK (Finger 4-8 area); resolved partially by 2021 disengagement, fully by Oct 2024 patrol agreement. STRATEGIC: northern bank features 'fingers' (mountain spurs) numbered 1-8 from west to east; India claims up to Finger 8, China up to Finger 4 — disputed area between fingers 4-8. UNIQUE FEATURE: water turns BLUE/GREEN/TURQUOISE depending on light + clouds; CINEMATIC fame from '3 IDIOTS' (2009 movie's climax filmed here at Pangong). FREEZES in winter (water saline but cold enough to freeze): solid ice from Nov-March. SPECIES: brown-headed gulls, Brahminy ducks; few fish (high salinity). ALTITUDE EFFECTS: oxygen ~60% of sea level; visitors warned about altitude sickness. PYQ FREQUENCY: Pangong-LAC in UPSC, SSC current affairs 1-2× per cycle.

cards.front:
DAL LAKE, the famous tourist lake of SRINAGAR, is fed primarily by which water source?

(A) Springs and snow-melt streams
(B) Direct rain water only here
(C) Underground aquifer flow only
(D) Glacial melt from far Tibet
cards.back:
(A) Springs and snow-melt streams

Rivers & Water Bodies — DAL LAKE — second-largest lake of Jammu & Kashmir; ~18 sq km; located in SRINAGAR. Sources: SPRINGS + MOUNTAIN STREAMS (Telbal Nallah, etc.) carrying SNOW-MELT from surrounding HIMALAYAN PEAKS (Mughal Garden hills, Shankaracharya Hill, Hari Parbat). FAMOUS FOR: (1) SHIKARAS — wooden gondolas; tourists ride. (2) HOUSEBOATS — opulent floating accommodations (a heritage from British era). (3) FLOATING GARDENS — vegetable-growing on rafts (locally called 'rad'). (4) MUGHAL GARDENS surrounding — Shalimar Bagh (Jahangir, 1619), Nishat Bagh (Nur Jahan's brother Asaf Khan, 1633), Chashma Shahi (Shah Jahan, 1632). (5) Centerpiece of Kashmir Valley tourism. POLLUTION: severely polluted by 1990s-2000s; sewage, encroachments, weeds (water-chestnut, lotus, pollutants). RESTORATION: Lakes & Waterways Development Authority (LAWDA, formed 1997) leading restoration. RECENT IMPROVEMENTS visible. DAL VS WULAR: DAL is in Srinagar, smaller, urban-touristic; WULAR is N. of Srinagar, much larger, less touristic, more biodiverse. KASHMIR VALLEY GEOGRAPHY: bowl-shaped, surrounded by Pir Panjal (S) and Greater Himalayas (N); JHELUM RIVER drains it. CULTURAL: 'Switzerland of India'. KEY POEMS: Allama Iqbal called Kashmir 'Heaven on Earth'. PYQ FREQUENCY: Dal Lake in SSC GA, UPSC tourism 1× per cycle.

cards.front:
INDIA's LARGEST lake by area, a SALTWATER coastal lagoon, is:

(A) Wular Lake, Kashmir's largest
(B) Chilika Lake, Odisha's coastal lagoon
(C) Sambhar Lake, of Rajasthan area
(D) Loktak Lake, of Manipur state
cards.back:
(B) Chilika Lake, Odisha's coastal lagoon

Rivers & Water Bodies — CHILIKA LAKE — Odisha's east coast. India's largest BRACKISH (slightly salty) coastal lagoon (~1100 sq km), and Asia's largest brackish lagoon. RAMSAR site (1981, India's first). Famous for: migratory birds (~150 species), Irrawaddy DOLPHINS. Source of livelihood for thousands of fishermen. SAMBHAR (Rajasthan) — India's largest INLAND saltwater lake, source of salt. WULAR (Kashmir) — India's largest FRESHWATER lake. LOKTAK (Manipur) — famous for unique floating PHUMDIS, home to endangered SANGAI deer.

WULAR LAKE, India's LARGEST FRESHWATER lake, is in:

(B) Jammu and Kashmir (Bandipore district)
(C) Uttarakhand, in the Garhwal region
(D) Sikkim, in the eastern Himalayan area
cards.back:
(B) Jammu and Kashmir (Bandipore district)

Rivers & Water Bodies — WULAR LAKE — north of Srinagar, in BANDIPORE district of Jammu + Kashmir. Largest freshwater lake in India (~125-200 sq km, varying with season). Fed by JHELUM river. RAMSAR site (1990). Important for Kashmir's fish supply. Other Kashmir lakes: DAL (boat-houses, shikara rides — Srinagar's most famous), NAGIN (close to Dal), MANASBAL (small, deepest in Kashmir). Distractor 1 — HP has Renuka, Bhrigu, Chandratal lakes. Distractor 3 — Uttarakhand has Naini, Bhimtal, Sat Tal.

cards.front:
GANGA river originates from which glacier?

(A) Gangotri glacier (Bhagirathi source)
(B) Yamunotri glacier (Yamuna source)
(C) Siachen glacier (Indus tributary)
(D) Zemu glacier (Teesta source)
cards.back:
(A) Gangotri glacier (Bhagirathi source)

Rivers & Water Bodies — GANGA river — TECHNICALLY the river is called 'BHAGIRATHI' from its source GANGOTRI GLACIER (snout: GAUMUKH, Uttarkashi district, Uttarakhand) until DEVPRAYAG, where it MERGES with the ALAKNANDA river to BECOME the GANGA. ALAKNANDA itself rises from SATOPANTH + BHAGIRATH KHARAK glaciers near Mana, Chamoli district. THE 'PANCH PRAYAG' (5 sacred confluences along Alaknanda) — VISHNUPRAYAG, NANDPRAYAG, KARNAPRAYAG, RUDRAPRAYAG, DEVPRAYAG — last one creates Ganga. GANGA's COURSE: Devprayag → Rishikesh → Haridwar (where it enters plains) → Kanpur → Allahabad/Prayagraj (joined by Yamuna at SANGAM) → Varanasi → Patna → Bhagalpur → enters Bangladesh as PADMA → meets Brahmaputra (called JAMUNA in Bangladesh) → MEGHNA → Bay of Bengal. TOTAL LENGTH: ~2,525 km (longest river WHOLLY in India... actually it spans India + Bangladesh; INDUS is longer but mostly outside India; BRAHMAPUTRA is also long but starts in Tibet). LARGEST DRAINAGE BASIN in India: Ganga ~10 lakh sq km; covers UP, MP, Uttarakhand, Bihar, Jharkhand, WB, Delhi, Rajasthan, Haryana. UPSC angle: NAMAMI GANGE PROGRAMME (2014-) — pollution abatement; Ganga Action Plan. PYQ FREQUENCY: Ganga source in SSC, UPSC, NDA 1× per cycle.

cards.front:
TRIVENI SANGAM at Allahabad/Prayagraj is the confluence of:

(A) Ganga, Yamuna, mythical Saraswati
(B) Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Indus
(C) Yamuna, Chambal, and Sone river
(D) Ganga, Bhagirathi, and Alaknanda
cards.back:
(A) Ganga, Yamuna, mythical Saraswati

Rivers & Water Bodies — TRIVENI SANGAM ('triple confluence') at PRAYAGRAJ (formerly Allahabad), Uttar Pradesh — confluence of: (1) GANGA — flowing from north (visible). (2) YAMUNA — flowing from west (visible). (3) SARASWATI — UNDERGROUND/MYTHICAL (not visible at surface; per legend, flows underground here). THIRD RIVER controversy: SARASWATI was a major Vedic river that DRIED UP ~4,000 BCE due to tectonic shifts (per geologists); identified with the Ghaggar-Hakra system. ATTRIBUTION VARIES: some say it's just spiritual presence; others say it actually emerges underground. KUMBH MELA: held at SANGAM every 12 YEARS (Maha Kumbh); ARDH KUMBH every 6 years; KUMBH ROTATES among 4 cities (PRAYAGRAJ, HARIDWAR, NASHIK, UJJAIN). PRAYAGRAJ 2025 KUMBH: ~40-60 crore pilgrims attended (largest peaceful gathering in human history). UNESCO recognized Kumbh Mela as INTANGIBLE CULTURAL HERITAGE OF HUMANITY (2017). HISTORICAL: AKBAR built FORT at Allahabad (1583) at confluence's strategic location — symbolic + strategic. FORT named ILAHABAD ('city of God'); renamed PRAYAGRAJ 2018 by UP government. UPSC angle: 'Saraswati' debates in NCERT history (Indus Valley civilization — was Harappan along Saraswati?). PYQ FREQUENCY: Triveni Sangam in SSC, UPSC, NDA 1× per cycle.

cards.front:
BRAHMAPUTRA river is known by which name in TIBET (its source)?

(A) Tsangpo (Yarlung Tsangpo)
(B) Mekong (a different river)
(C) Salween (a different river)
(D) Indus (different basin)
cards.back:
(A) Tsangpo (Yarlung Tsangpo)

Rivers & Water Bodies — BRAHMAPUTRA — known by DIFFERENT NAMES through its course: (1) TIBET — YARLUNG TSANGPO (source: CHEMAYUNGDUNG glacier near Mt KAILASH, Tibet). Flows EASTWARD across S. Tibet for ~1,700 km (highest river in world by altitude). (2) Takes a U-TURN at NAMCHA BARWA peak (~7,800 m), forming the WORLD'S DEEPEST CANYON (Yarlung Tsangpo Grand Canyon). (3) ARUNACHAL PRADESH (India) — called SIANG (as it enters India from north). (4) ASSAM — called BRAHMAPUTRA after merging with Dibang + Lohit at Sadiya. (5) BANGLADESH — called JAMUNA (different from Yamuna of north India!). (6) MERGES with PADMA (= Ganga in Bangladesh) at Goalondo → joint river called PADMA-JAMUNA. (7) MEGHNA — final stretch, into Bay of Bengal. TOTAL LENGTH: ~2,900 km (~700 km in India). LARGEST RIVER BY VOLUME in India (~1.5× Ganga's flow at Bay of Bengal). MAJOR FLOOD CHALLENGES — Assam annually devastated by Brahmaputra floods. KAZIRANGA NP gets ~80% inundated yearly. CHINA'S DAM CONCERNS: China is building MEGA DAMS on Tsangpo (e.g., 60-GW Medog dam, world's largest hydro project planned) — INDIA worries about water flow + flash-floods. NEPAL-BANGLADESH-INDIA water diplomacy concerns. UPSC angle: TRANSBOUNDARY RIVERS, water security; GS-2 IR with China, Bangladesh. PYQ FREQUENCY: Brahmaputra-Tsangpo link in UPSC, SSC 1-2× per cycle.

cards.front:
INDUS WATERS TREATY (1960) was signed between INDIA and PAKISTAN with mediation by:

(A) World Bank (IBRD)
(B) United Nations (UN)
(C) International Court of Justice (ICJ)
(D) Saudi Arabia (mediator)
cards.back:
(A) World Bank (IBRD)

Rivers & Water Bodies — INDUS WATERS TREATY (IWT) — signed 19 SEPTEMBER 1960 in KARACHI by PM JAWAHARLAL NEHRU (India) and President AYUB KHAN (Pakistan). MEDIATOR: WORLD BANK (IBRD) — facilitated negotiations + provided technical assistance. KEY ALLOCATION: INDUS BASIN has 6 main rivers; treaty divides them: (1) EASTERN RIVERS (RAVI, BEAS, SUTLEJ) — fully to INDIA. (2) WESTERN RIVERS (INDUS, JHELUM, CHENAB) — substantially to PAKISTAN, with India having LIMITED USE rights (drinking, navigation, run-of-river hydropower without storage). KEY PROVISIONS: (a) PERMANENT INDUS COMMISSION — meets at least once a year. (b) DISPUTE RESOLUTION mechanism: bilateral commission → Neutral Expert → Court of Arbitration. (c) Treaty has SURVIVED FOUR WARS between India-Pakistan (1965, 1971, 1999 Kargil, near-war 2019, 2025) — testament to international water-treaty resilience. RECENT TENSIONS: (1) Pakistan complaints about KISHENGANGA (Jhelum tributary) and RATLE (Chenab) hydroelectric projects. (2) INDIA'S 2025 SUSPENSION/MODIFICATION threats post-Pahalgam terror attack — major diplomatic event. UPSC ANGLE: bilateral water treaties — treated extensively in GS-2 IR + GS-3 environment. OTHER WATER TREATIES: (a) GANGA TREATY 1996 with Bangladesh (Farakka water-sharing). (b) MAHAKALI TREATY 1996 with Nepal. (c) TEESTA — pending with Bangladesh. PYQ FREQUENCY: IWT in UPSC PT, Mains GS-2/3 1× per cycle.

cards.front:
Which is the LONGEST river of PENINSULAR INDIA?

(A) Godavari ('Dakshin Ganga')
(B) Krishna (2nd longest peninsular)
(C) Kaveri (4th by length)
(D) Narmada (west-flowing largest)
cards.back:
(A) Godavari ('Dakshin Ganga')

Rivers & Water Bodies — GODAVARI — LONGEST river of PENINSULAR INDIA; ~1,465 km. Called 'DAKSHIN GANGA' ('Ganga of the South'). SOURCE: TRYAMBAKESHWAR, Nashik district, MAHARASHTRA (in Western Ghats). FLOWS EASTWARD through MH, Telangana, AP into BAY OF BENGAL at delta near KAKINADA (AP). MAJOR TRIBUTARIES: Manjira, Pravara, Indravati, Wardha, Wainganga, Penganga, Sabari. DAMS: Polavaram (under construction, AP), Sriram Sagar, Pochampad, Jayakwadi. PENINSULAR RIVER LENGTHS (memorize): (1) GODAVARI — 1,465 km (longest). (2) KRISHNA — 1,400 km. (3) MAHANADI — 851 km (Odisha + CG). (4) KAVERI — 800 km. (5) NARMADA — 1,312 km (longest WEST-FLOWING peninsular; into Arabian Sea via Gulf of Khambhat). (6) TAPI — 724 km (also west-flowing). EAST-FLOWING vs WEST-FLOWING peninsular rivers: most east (Bay of Bengal); narrow Western Ghats divert SOME west (Narmada, Tapi, Mahi, Sabarmati, Periyar, Sharavathi). EAST-FLOWING form deltas (Krishna-Godavari is fertile rice-bowl); WEST-FLOWING form ESTUARIES (steep gradient, no deltas). UPSC angle: peninsular drainage system in NCERT class 9-10 + Indian Geography optional. CRITICAL: Krishna-Godavari basin is INDIA's RICE BOWL — MAJOR REGION for paddy, sugarcane. POLAVARAM PROJECT — multi-state project on Godavari, contentious. PYQ FREQUENCY: peninsular rivers in SSC, UPSC, NDA 1-2× per cycle.

cards.front:
The NARMADA river flows through a unique geological feature called a:

(A) Rift valley (between Vindhya and Satpura)
(B) Glacial valley (in mountains) (option here)
(C) Coastal plain (delta region) (option here)
(D) Alluvial floodplain (uniform) (option here)
cards.back:
(A) Rift valley (between Vindhya and Satpura)

Rivers & Water Bodies — NARMADA flows through a RIFT VALLEY between the VINDHYA RANGE (north) and SATPURA RANGE (south). RIFT VALLEY: tectonic feature where land between two parallel faults has dropped down (graben). NARMADA is INDIA's only major river flowing in a rift valley. CONSEQUENCE: short tributaries (mountains close on both sides), no significant delta (steep gradient + estuary instead). LENGTH: ~1,312 km — INDIA's 5th longest river overall, LONGEST WEST-FLOWING peninsular river. SOURCE: AMARKANTAK plateau in MP (also source of Sone, which flows east). MOUTH: GULF OF KHAMBHAT (Arabian Sea), near Bharuch (Gujarat). KEY DAMS: SARDAR SAROVAR DAM (Gujarat, completed 2017 after decades of agitation); INDIRA SAGAR (MP); OMKARESHWAR + Mahesh­war + Bargi. NARMADA BACHAO ANDOLAN (NBA) — led by MEDHA PATKAR since 1989 — landmark social movement against Sardar Sarovar's height; argued for tribal rehabilitation, environmental concerns. SC ruled 2000 allowing dam to proceed (with monitoring). NARMADA's CULTURAL/RELIGIOUS importance: 'PARIKRAMA' (circumambulation) of Narmada is a sacred Hindu pilgrimage — ~3,500 km walk along both banks; takes 3-4 years. UPSC GEOGRAPHY: tectonic features in Indian peninsula — Aravalli (oldest); Vindhya + Satpura horst-graben system; Western/Eastern Ghats. PYQ FREQUENCY: Narmada rift valley in UPSC, SSC, NDA 1× per cycle.

cards.front:
The 'NATIONAL RIVER' of India, declared in 2008, is:

(A) Ganga (Namami Gange focus)
(B) Yamuna (cleanest priority)
(C) Brahmaputra (Assam mainstay)
(D) Godavari (Dakshin Ganga)
cards.back:
(A) Ganga (Namami Gange focus)

Rivers & Water Bodies — GANGA — declared 'NATIONAL RIVER OF INDIA' in NOVEMBER 2008 by then-PM Manmohan Singh. KEY EVENTS regarding Ganga: (1) 1986 — GANGA ACTION PLAN (GAP) launched by Rajiv Gandhi govt. (2) 2008 — declared National River. (3) 2009 — NATIONAL GANGA RIVER BASIN AUTHORITY (NGRBA) established. (4) 2011 — World Bank loan for cleanup. (5) 2014 — NAMAMI GANGE Programme launched by Modi govt — ~₹20,000 crore initial; cleaning, ghats, sewage treatment, biodiversity, public participation. KEY POLLUTION SOURCES: (a) Untreated SEWAGE from cities (~2,500 MLD discharged into Ganga; only ~50% treated). (b) INDUSTRIAL effluents — tanneries (Kanpur), chemicals, textile. (c) AGRICULTURAL runoff — pesticides, fertilizers. (d) Religious offerings — flowers, plastics, ashes. RIVER GANGA BASIN: covers ~26% of India; populated by ~50 crore people; supports vast agriculture. NATIONAL AQUATIC ANIMAL: GANGES RIVER DOLPHIN (Platanista gangetica) — declared 2009; endangered; lives in Ganga + Brahmaputra. WORLD RIVERS DAY: 4th Sunday of September. INDIAN RIVERS UPSC angle: NAMAMI GANGE achievements + criticisms; biodiversity; tribal rights; transboundary water sharing. NATIONAL WATERWAYS — Ganga is NW-1 (Allahabad to Haldia, 1,620 km — used for cargo). PYQ FREQUENCY: Ganga as National River in UPSC, SSC, NDA, MPSC 1× per cycle.

cards.front:
The longest river in India is the:

(A) Brahmaputra
(B) Ganga
(C) Godavari
(D) Narmada
cards.back:
(B) Ganga

Rivers & Water Bodies — The Ganga — ~2,525 km — is the longest river flowing mainly within India. The Brahmaputra is longer overall (~2,900 km) but most of its length is in Tibet and Bangladesh. The Godavari (~1,465 km) is the longest river of peninsular India and is called the 'Dakshin Ganga'. Narmada (~1,312 km) flows westwards into the Arabian Sea through a rift valley.

cards.front:
The Ganga river originates as the 'Bhagirathi' from a glacier called:

(A) Milam glacier
(B) Gangotri glacier
(C) Pindari glacier
(D) Siachen glacier
cards.back:
(B) Gangotri glacier

Rivers & Water Bodies — The Bhagirathi emerges from the Gangotri glacier at Gaumukh, Uttarakhand (~4,100 m). It joins the Alaknanda at Devprayag to form the Ganga. The other 'prayags' (confluences on the upper Ganga): Vishnuprayag, Nandprayag, Karnaprayag, Rudraprayag, Devprayag ('panch prayag'). Siachen is the source of the Nubra river (a Shyok tributary of the Indus).

cards.front:
Which of the following rivers flows through a rift valley?

(A) Ganga
(B) Narmada
(C) Godavari
(D) Krishna
cards.back:
(B) Narmada

Rivers & Water Bodies — The Narmada (and the Tapi) flow through rift valleys — linear depressions between parallel mountain ranges (Vindhya to the north, Satpura to the south). They flow westwards into the Arabian Sea — exceptions among the mostly east-flowing peninsular rivers. Most rivers of the peninsula (Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, Mahanadi) flow east into the Bay of Bengal and form deltas.

cards.front:
The Brahmaputra river enters India from Arunachal Pradesh, where it is locally called:

(A) Tsangpo
(B) Siang (or Dihang)
(C) Jamuna
(D) Padma
cards.back:
(B) Siang (or Dihang)

Rivers & Water Bodies — The Brahmaputra system — in Tibet called Tsangpo; enters India as the Siang / Dihang in Arunachal Pradesh; becomes the Brahmaputra in Assam after joining the Lohit and Dibang near Sadiya; in Bangladesh called Jamuna (not to be confused with Yamuna of the Ganga basin); joins the Padma (Ganga's name in Bangladesh) and the Meghna before emptying into the Bay of Bengal.

cards.front:
The largest tributary of the Ganga (by catchment area) is the:

(A) Yamuna
(B) Gandak
(C) Kosi
(D) Son
cards.back:
(A) Yamuna

Rivers & Water Bodies — The Yamuna — rising from Yamunotri — is the largest tributary of the Ganga by both length (~1,375 km) and catchment area. It joins the Ganga at Prayagraj (Allahabad) in the 'Triveni Sangam' (with the mythological Saraswati). Other major Ganga tributaries — Ramganga, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi (from the Himalayan north), and Chambal, Betwa, Son (from the Vindhya/Satpura south).

cards.front:
The river sacred to the Sikhs as the 'River of the Punjab', flowing past Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple) — via Amritsar, is the:

(A) Sutlej
(B) Ravi
(C) Beas
(D) Chenab
cards.back:
(B) Ravi

Rivers & Water Bodies — The Ravi flows near Amritsar; the sarovar of the Golden Temple is fed by it (and by groundwater). The five rivers of the Punjab — Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej — give the region its name ('panj' = five + 'aab' = water). All five are tributaries of the Indus. Under the Indus Waters Treaty (1960), Pakistan gets full use of the three western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) and India of the three eastern (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej).

cards.front:
Which is the TALLEST single-drop waterfall in INDIA?

(A) Kunchikal Falls (Karnataka, ~455 m)
(B) Jog Falls of the Sharavathi
(C) Dudhsagar Falls in Goa-Karnataka
(D) Athirappilly Falls in Kerala
cards.back:
(A) Kunchikal Falls (Karnataka, ~455 m)

Rivers & Water Bodies — KUNCHIKAL FALLS — INDIA's TALLEST WATERFALL with cumulative drop of ~455 m (1,493 ft). Located in SHIMOGA district, KARNATAKA, on the VARAHI river (a Karnataka river). It's a 'TIERED' waterfall (drops in stages, not single-leap). RANKING — TALLEST WATERFALLS in INDIA (heights approximate, tiered drops): (1) KUNCHIKAL — 455 m (Karnataka, Varahi river). (2) BARKANA FALLS — 259 m (Karnataka, on Seeta river). (3) NOHKALIKAI FALLS — 340 m single drop (Meghalaya, Cherrapunji area) — many sources call this India's TALLEST PLUNGE WATERFALL. (4) NOHSNGITHIANG (Seven Sisters Falls) — 315 m (Meghalaya). (5) DUDHSAGAR — 310 m (Goa-Karnataka, Mandovi river). (6) JOG FALLS — 253 m (Karnataka, Sharavathi river — most FAMOUS). (7) ATHIRAPPILLY — 25 m (Kerala, Chalakudy — 'Niagara of India'). NOTE: 'tallest' depends on whether you count single drop or total tiered drop. NOHKALIKAI is sometimes claimed as tallest single-plunge (340m). Question/answer convention varies by source. JOG FALLS — 4 segments: RAJA, RANI, ROCKET, ROARER — most popular tourist waterfall. PYQ FREQUENCY: tallest waterfall is a top SSC GA, UPSC, NDA fact — 1× per cycle.

cards.front:
JOG FALLS, the famous waterfall in Karnataka, is on which river?

(A) Sharavathi River (West-flowing)
(B) Kaveri River (in southern part)
(C) Krishna River (peninsular India)
(D) Tungabhadra River (in central)
cards.back:
(A) Sharavathi River (West-flowing)

Rivers & Water Bodies — JOG FALLS — on the SHARAVATHI RIVER, in the WESTERN GHATS, SHIMOGA district, Karnataka. River SHARAVATHI is a WEST-FLOWING river (drains into Arabian Sea at Honnavar). HEIGHT: ~253 m (829 ft). FOUR SEGMENTS (named with personalities): (1) RAJA (the 'King') — flows uninterrupted. (2) RANI (the 'Queen') — meanders gently. (3) ROARER — flows turbulently into deep gorge. (4) ROCKET — bursts out at high velocity. MONSOON SEASON (Jun-Sep) — most spectacular; in summer the volume is reduced due to upstream LINGANAMAKKI dam (built 1964 for Mahatma Gandhi Hydroelectric Project). KEY HYDRO PROJECT: Sharavathi Hydro Project — 1,469 MW capacity, one of India's earliest large hydropower stations. ALTERNATE NAMES: Jog is also known as GERSOPPA FALLS (after old downstream village) or JOGADA GUNDI. KEY GEOGRAPHIC INSIGHT — WEST-FLOWING vs EAST-FLOWING rivers in peninsula: West-flowing (Narmada, Tapi, Sharavathi, Periyar, Mandovi) drain to ARABIAN SEA; have STEEP gradient → many WATERFALLS. East-flowing (Krishna, Godavari, Kaveri, Mahanadi) drain to BAY OF BENGAL; flatter → DELTAS (e.g., Krishna-Godavari delta in AP). PYQ FREQUENCY: Jog-Sharavathi link is a top SSC, UPSC, KAS fact — 1× per cycle.

cards.front:
DUDHSAGAR FALLS, often featured in Bollywood films like 'Chennai Express', is located on the border of:

(A) Goa and Karnataka states
(B) Maharashtra and Karnataka borders
(C) Kerala and Tamil Nadu junction
(D) Andhra Pradesh and Telangana side
cards.back:
(A) Goa and Karnataka states

Rivers & Water Bodies — DUDHSAGAR FALLS — on the MANDOVI RIVER, on the GOA-KARNATAKA border. Total drop ~310 m, in 4 tiers; INDIA's 4th-5th tallest waterfall depending on ranking method. NAME: 'Dudhsagar' = 'sea of milk' in Marathi/Konkani — the milky-white cascade resembles flowing milk. Located in BHAGWAN MAHAVEER WILDLIFE SANCTUARY + MOLLEM NATIONAL PARK. ACCESSIBLE BY: (1) Train (Konkan Railway passes near; the falls are visible from the train — iconic shot from 'Chennai Express' 2013, where Shahrukh Khan + Deepika Padukone climbed onto the train near the falls — NOT recommended IRL!). (2) Trek from Castle Rock (~12 km). (3) Jeep + boat from Goa side. (4) Train stop briefly at Dudhsagar station (Indian Railways stopped this in 2014 for safety after several deaths). MANDOVI RIVER — Goa's main river; flows through Goa's capital PANAJI (= Panjim), into Arabian Sea. SHARES TYPE: like Jog, Dudhsagar is a WESTERN GHATS waterfall on a WEST-FLOWING river. KONKAN RAILWAY — engineering marvel — runs along the western coast, opened 1998; spans 760 km from Roha (Maharashtra) to Mangaluru (Karnataka). PYQ FREQUENCY: Dudhsagar in Geography MCQs of SSC, IBPS GA — 1× per cycle.

cards.front:
ATHIRAPPILLY FALLS, called 'Niagara of India', is in which state?

(A) Kerala (on the Chalakudy river)
(B) Karnataka of southern India
(C) Tamil Nadu state directly south
(D) Andhra Pradesh state of east
cards.back:
(A) Kerala (on the Chalakudy river)

Rivers & Water Bodies — ATHIRAPPILLY FALLS — KERALA's largest waterfall, on the CHALAKUDY RIVER, in THRISSUR district. HEIGHT: ~25 m, but its WIDTH (330 m at full flow during monsoon) gives it 'Niagara of India' moniker. LOCATION: Western Ghats foothills, ~70 km from Kochi. ECOSYSTEM: VAZHACHAL Forest Division — biodiverse rainforest; home to several ENDEMIC HORNBILLS (Great Hornbill, Malabar Pied Hornbill, Indian Grey Hornbill, Malabar Grey Hornbill). FILMS: Bahubali (Telugu, 2015) shot the iconic waterfall scenes here; Dil Se (Hindi, 1998), Vinodayathra (Malayalam), Punarvasu (Tamil) — many films showcased Athirappilly. CONTROVERSY: a proposed ATHIRAPPILLY HYDROELECTRIC PROJECT (163 MW) has been DEBATED since 1990s. Environmentalists oppose due to wildlife damage; State govt has stalled it; latest reports (2024) suggest plans dropped. CHALAKUDY RIVER — flows from Anamalai Hills (Western Ghats) into ARABIAN SEA; total length ~145 km. NEAR ATTRACTIONS: VAZHACHAL Falls (downstream from Athirappilly), CHARPA Falls. KERALA TOURISM markets these as 'God's Own Country' essential visits. PYQ FREQUENCY: 'Niagara of India' tag in SSC GA, UPSC, KAS — 1× per cycle.

cards.front:
HOGENAKKAL FALLS, called 'Niagara of South India', is on which river?

(A) Kaveri River (Tamil Nadu)
(B) Krishna River (further north)
(C) Godavari River (eastern flow)
(D) Tungabhadra River (Krishna's)
cards.back:
(A) Kaveri River (Tamil Nadu)

Rivers & Water Bodies — HOGENAKKAL FALLS — on the KAVERI RIVER, on the TAMIL NADU-KARNATAKA BORDER (Dharmapuri district, TN). Multi-channel cataract — water cascades through hundreds of small streams over rocks. NAME: 'Hogenakkal' in Kannada = 'smoking rocks' (mist creates smoke-like illusion). HEIGHT: ~20 m, but WIDTH and VOLUME are impressive. ATTRACTIONS: (1) CORACLE BOAT RIDES (round wicker-and-leather boats) for tourists — distinctive. (2) Therapeutic FISH SPA (small fish nibble dead skin — natural pedicure). (3) FRESH RIVER FISH cooked in coconut-based curries — specialty. KAVERI RIVER (also Cauvery): rises in TALAKAVERI (Brahmagiri Hills, KARNATAKA); flows through Karnataka, Tamil Nadu (~800 km); empties at POOMPUHAR delta into BAY OF BENGAL. KAVERI WATER DISPUTE: long-running between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu — Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal (1990); SC verdict 2018 finalized water-sharing. KEY KAVERI BASIN: Mekedatu reservoir proposal (Karnataka) is contested by Tamil Nadu. RELATED FALLS on KAVERI: Shivanasamudra Falls (Karnataka, ~98 m, twin falls — Bharachukki and Gaganachukki), generates 4,800 MW hydroelectricity. PYQ FREQUENCY: Hogenakkal-Kaveri link in SSC GA, UPSC 1× per cycle.
