cards.front:
The LONGEST RIVER in the world is (by most modern measurements):

(A) Amazon (~6,400 km — disputed in recent studies)
(B) Yangtze (~6,300 km, Asia’s longest)
(C) NILE (~6,650 km, Africa) — traditional ranking; flows N through 11 countries into the Mediterranean Sea; some 2023 studies suggest Amazon may be slightly longer
(D) Mississippi-Missouri (~6,275 km)
cards.back:
(C) NILE (~6,650 km, Africa) — traditional ranking; flows N through 11 countries into the Mediterranean Sea; some 2023 studies suggest Amazon may be slightly longer

World Geography — NILE — traditionally considered LONGEST river; ~6,650 km from its deepest source (LAKE VICTORIA, or further tributaries in RWANDA / BURUNDI / ETHIOPIA highlands) to the MEDITERRANEAN Sea delta in EGYPT. Flows NORTH through 11 countries: BURUNDI, RWANDA, TANZANIA, UGANDA, DR CONGO, KENYA, ETHIOPIA, SOUTH SUDAN, SUDAN, EGYPT, ERITREA (basin). Two MAJOR TRIBUTARIES: (1) WHITE NILE — source Lake Victoria; longer, colder; (2) BLUE NILE — source Lake Tana (Ethiopia); supplies ~85% of water + silt during floods; the two meet at KHARTOUM (Sudan). Gives rise to ancient Egyptian civilisation; ASWAN HIGH DAM (1970) built on it; creates LAKE NASSER. 2007 & 2023 studies using GPS and satellite re-measurement suggest the AMAZON (Peru to Atlantic, Brazil) may be ~6,992 km, slightly LONGER than Nile — so the question is increasingly contested. AMAZON is undisputedly: (1) LARGEST BY DISCHARGE (Volume) — 209,000 m³/s, nearly 5x Congo (next biggest); (2) largest DRAINAGE BASIN (~7 million sq km); (3) widest river. OTHER TOP RIVERS: YANGTZE (6,300 km, longest in Asia, China), MISSISSIPPI-MISSOURI (USA), YENISEI (Russia), YELLOW / HUANG HE (China), OB (Russia), PARANA (S America), CONGO (2nd by discharge), AMUR (Russia-China), LENA (Russia).

cards.front:
Which is the LARGEST FRESHWATER lake in the world by area?

(A) Caspian Sea (largest but saline)
(B) Lake Baikal (Siberia, Russia) — largest by VOLUME, deepest in the world
(C) LAKE SUPERIOR (Great Lakes, USA-Canada border) — 82,100 sq km — largest FRESHWATER lake by SURFACE AREA
(D) Lake Victoria (Africa)
cards.back:
(C) LAKE SUPERIOR (Great Lakes, USA-Canada border) — 82,100 sq km — largest FRESHWATER lake by SURFACE AREA

World Geography — LAKE SUPERIOR — largest FRESHWATER LAKE in the world BY AREA (82,100 sq km); one of 5 GREAT LAKES (SUPERIOR, MICHIGAN, HURON, ERIE, ONTARIO — mnemonic ‘SMHEO’ or ‘HOMES’); bordered by CANADA (Ontario) to the north and USA (Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan) to the south. CASPIAN SEA (371,000 sq km) is LARGER but is a SALTWATER endorheic ‘sea’ (saline); technically the world's largest inland BODY of water. Among freshwater by surface area: SUPERIOR > VICTORIA (Africa, 68,800 — largest IN AFRICA, 3rd-largest world freshwater) > HURON > MICHIGAN > TANGANYIKA (E. Africa, 2nd-largest by volume, deepest in Africa 1,470 m). By VOLUME: (1) CASPIAN (saline); by FRESHWATER volume: (1) BAIKAL (Russia/Siberia) — holds 22-23% of world's freshwater, 1,642 m deep (deepest in world, OLDEST at 25-30 million years, UNESCO WHS); (2) TANGANYIKA; (3) SUPERIOR. DEEPEST: BAIKAL (1,642 m). HIGHEST navigable: TITICACA (Bolivia-Peru border, 3,812 m). LOWEST ELEVATION lake: DEAD SEA (-430 m below sea level, 34% salinity — one of saltiest). LARGEST IN INDIA: WULAR (J&K, freshwater, tectonic); LARGEST SALTWATER in India: CHILIKA (Odisha, brackish). LARGEST ARTIFICIAL LAKE: KARIBA (Zimbabwe-Zambia).
cards.option2: Lake Baikal (Siberia, Russia) — largest by VOLUME, deepest in the world

cards.front:
The EQUATOR passes through the LARGEST NUMBER OF COUNTRIES on which continent?

(A) Asia (passes through Indonesia)
(B) AFRICA — equator passes through 7 African countries (São Tomé & Príncipe, Gabon, Republic of Congo, DR Congo, Uganda, Kenya, Somalia)
(C) South America (passes through Ecuador, Colombia, Brazil)
(D) Oceania (passes through Kiribati)
cards.back:
(B) AFRICA — equator passes through 7 African countries (São Tomé & Príncipe, Gabon, Republic of Congo, DR Congo, Uganda, Kenya, Somalia)

World Geography — EQUATOR (0° latitude) — passes through 13 COUNTRIES in total globally. AFRICA has the MOST — 7 countries: (1) SÃO TOMÉ & PRÍNCIPE (island, off W. Africa), (2) GABON, (3) REPUBLIC OF THE CONGO, (4) DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO (DRC), (5) UGANDA, (6) KENYA, (7) SOMALIA (through territorial waters). SOUTH AMERICA: 3 countries — ECUADOR (named after equator!), COLOMBIA, BRAZIL. ASIA: 2 countries — INDONESIA (passes through Borneo/Kalimantan, Sumatra), MALDIVES (small islands straddle). OCEANIA: 1 — KIRIBATI (passes through some islands). TOTAL: 7+3+2+1 = 13. TROPIC OF CANCER (23.5° N) — passes through MEXICO, BAHAMAS, WESTERN SAHARA, MAURITANIA, MALI, ALGERIA, NIGER, LIBYA, EGYPT, SAUDI ARABIA, UAE, OMAN, INDIA (8 Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram), BANGLADESH, MYANMAR, CHINA, TAIWAN. In INDIA, Tropic of Cancer is a useful mnemonic for ‘8 states through which it passes’. TROPIC OF CAPRICORN (23.5° S) — passes through AUSTRALIA, CHILE, ARGENTINA, PARAGUAY, BRAZIL, NAMIBIA, BOTSWANA, S. AFRICA, MOZAMBIQUE, MADAGASCAR. INTERNATIONAL DATE LINE roughly follows 180° meridian through the Pacific, deviating to avoid landmasses.

cards.front:
Which ocean is the SMALLEST and SHALLOWEST of the world's five oceans?

(A) Indian Ocean
(B) Atlantic Ocean
(C) Southern (Antarctic) Ocean
(D) ARCTIC OCEAN
cards.back:
(D) ARCTIC OCEAN

World Geography — ARCTIC OCEAN — SMALLEST and SHALLOWEST of the world's 5 oceans. DIMENSIONS: Surface area ~14.06 million sq km (vs Pacific 165 M); avg depth ~1,200 m (vs Pacific avg 4,280 m). BORDERED BY 8 ARCTIC COUNTRIES: USA (Alaska), Canada, Denmark (Greenland), Iceland, Norway, Sweden, Finland, Russia. FEATURES: (1) largely COVERED by SEA ICE year-round (shrinking due to climate change — Arctic sea ice minimum in September each year); (2) the NORTH POLE sits in its centre, on floating ice, not land; (3) contains the NORTH GEOGRAPHIC POLE; (4) home to Inuit, polar bears, seals, walruses, whales. WORLD’S 5 OCEANS (by size, LARGEST → SMALLEST): (1) PACIFIC (~165.25M sq km, nearly 1/3 of Earth) — DEEPEST; contains Mariana Trench; (2) ATLANTIC (~106.46M) — S-shaped; contains Puerto Rico Trench; Sargasso Sea; (3) INDIAN (~70.56M); warmest; contains Java Trench; (4) SOUTHERN / ANTARCTIC (~20.33M) — surrounds Antarctica up to 60°S (recognised as distinct 5th ocean by IHO 2000, by National Geographic 2021); contains Antarctic Circumpolar Current (largest ocean current); (5) ARCTIC (~14.06M) — smallest, shallowest, coldest. All connect — one world ocean. COVER ~71% of Earth's surface. ~14.06 million sq km; bordered by 8 countries; partly ice-covered year-round; avg depth ~1,200 m.

cards.front:
The GREAT BARRIER REEF, the world's largest coral reef system, is located off the coast of:

(A) Mexico (Caribbean)
(B) QUEENSLAND, AUSTRALIA
(C) Fiji
(D) Philippines
cards.back:
(B) QUEENSLAND, AUSTRALIA

World Geography — GREAT BARRIER REEF — World's LARGEST coral reef system; stretches ~2,300 km (1,400 mi) along the north-eastern coast of AUSTRALIA (mostly off the coast of QUEENSLAND), in the CORAL SEA (western Pacific). COMPRISES 2,900+ individual reefs, 900+ islands. VISIBLE FROM SPACE — the largest structure built by living organisms on Earth. HOME TO: 1,500 fish species, 411 coral types, 134 sharks/rays, dugongs, humpback whales, 6 turtle species. UNESCO WORLD HERITAGE (1981). THREATS: coral bleaching (due to ocean warming), agri runoff, crown-of-thorns starfish — multiple mass bleaching events in 2016, 2017, 2020, 2022, 2024. OTHER MAJOR REEFS: (1) BELIZE BARRIER REEF (Central America, 2nd largest, UNESCO); (2) NEW CALEDONIA BARRIER REEF (Pacific, 3rd); (3) RED SEA reefs; (4) INDIAN REEFS — LAKSHADWEEP (atolls, only coral atolls of India), GULF OF MANNAR, GULF OF KUTCH, ANDAMAN & NICOBAR, MALVAN (Maharashtra). CORAL REEFS form in shallow (<100 m) warm (20-28°C) tropical seas; need sunlight (zooxanthellae photosynthesis). Types: FRINGING (close to shore), BARRIER (separated by lagoon), ATOLL (ring-shaped, around submerged volcano island — e.g. Lakshadweep, Maldives). stretches ~2,300 km; visible from space; UNESCO site 1981; in the Coral Sea.

cards.front:
The ‘Ring of Fire’, a belt known for intense volcanic and seismic activity, is associated with the:

(A) Atlantic Ocean
(B) Mediterranean-Himalayan belt
(C) PACIFIC OCEAN
(D) Indian Ocean
cards.back:
(C) PACIFIC OCEAN

World Geography — PACIFIC RING OF FIRE (also ‘Circum-Pacific Belt’) — a horseshoe-shaped ZONE, ~40,000 km in length, encircling the PACIFIC OCEAN; characterised by intense TECTONIC activity: (1) ~75% of world’s ACTIVE (and dormant) VOLCANOES — ~450 of 850; (2) ~90% of world’s EARTHQUAKES; (3) the world’s largest earthquakes happen here — e.g., Chile 1960 (M 9.5, largest ever recorded), Alaska 1964 (M 9.2), Sumatra 2004 (M 9.1, caused Indian Ocean tsunami), Japan Tōhoku 2011 (M 9.1). CAUSED BY: numerous SUBDUCTION zones — Pacific plate, Nazca plate, Cocos plate, Juan de Fuca, Philippine, Indo-Australian plates — all dive beneath continental plates, creating trenches + arcs of volcanoes + frequent seismicity. COUNTRIES ON THE RING: New Zealand, Tonga, Papua New Guinea, Indonesia, Philippines, Taiwan, Japan, Russia (Kamchatka), Aleutian Islands (USA), Alaska (USA), western Canada, western USA (California), Mexico, Guatemala, Costa Rica, Panama, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Chile. Famous volcanoes on the Ring: FUJI (Japan), PINATUBO (Philippines, erupted 1991), KRAKATOA (Indonesia, 1883), MERAPI (Indonesia), MT. ST. HELENS (USA, 1980), POPOCATÉPETL (Mexico), COTOPAXI (Ecuador), MAUNA LOA (Hawaii). SECONDARY BELT: the ALPINE-HIMALAYAN / MEDITERRANEAN belt (~17% of earthquakes) — includes Himalayas, Iran, Turkey, Italy (Mt Etna, Vesuvius). a horseshoe-shaped belt around the Pacific where ~75% of world's active volcanoes and ~90% of earthquakes occur, due to subduction at plate margins.

cards.front:
The ANGEL FALLS, the highest uninterrupted waterfall in the world, is located in:

(A) Brazil (Iguazu)
(B) Canada-USA border (Niagara)
(C) VENEZUELA — in Canaima National Park; 979 m (3,212 ft) total drop; named after US pilot Jimmie Angel (1933)
(D) Zimbabwe-Zambia border (Victoria)
cards.back:
(C) VENEZUELA — in Canaima National Park; 979 m (3,212 ft) total drop; named after US pilot Jimmie Angel (1933)

World Geography — ANGEL FALLS (Spanish: ‘Salto Ángel’; indigenous Pemon: ‘KEREPAKUPAI MERÚ’ = ‘Waterfall of the Deepest Place’) — HIGHEST UNINTERRUPTED WATERFALL in the world. TOTAL HEIGHT: 979 m (3,212 ft); uninterrupted single drop: 807 m (2,648 ft). LOCATION: AUYÁN-TEPUI mountain, CANAIMA NATIONAL PARK (UNESCO World Heritage), BOLÍVAR STATE, VENEZUELA. Named after JIMMIE ANGEL, the American aviator who first flew over them in 1933 and crash-landed on top in 1937. The water plunges from a flat-topped TEPUI mountain into a gorge. The falls inspired ‘Paradise Falls’ in the animated film UP (Pixar, 2009). OTHER WATERFALLS of note: (1) VICTORIA FALLS (Mosi-oa-Tunya = ‘smoke that thunders’) — Zambia/Zimbabwe border, 108 m high but WIDEST curtain at 1,708 m, explorer David Livingstone named it 1855; (2) NIAGARA FALLS — USA/Canada, 51 m, but highest WATER VOLUME; (3) IGUAZU FALLS — Brazil/Argentina, 82 m, 275 cascades, ‘Niagara on steroids’; (4) TUGELA FALLS — South Africa, 948 m (some argue highest if cascaded drops counted). INDIA’S HIGHEST WATERFALLS: KUNCHIKAL (Karnataka, 455 m, tallest in India), JOG (Karnataka, 253 m), DUDHSAGAR (Goa-Karnataka border, 310 m).

(A) Mount Kilimanjaro
(B) Mount Everest
(C) K2

cards.back:
(B) Mount Everest

The LARGEST desert in the world (by area) is:

(A) Sahara
(B) Antarctica
(C) Gobi
(D) Thar
cards.back:
(B) Antarctica

World Geography — Antarctica is technically a polar desert (very low precipitation) covering ~14.2 million sq km — the largest desert. Sahara (~9.2 million sq km) is the largest HOT desert. Desert definition: <25 cm annual precipitation.

(A) Tropic of Cancer
(B) Prime Meridian
(C) International Date Line
(D) Equator
cards.back:
(B) Prime Meridian

World Geography — Prime Meridian — 0° longitude, passes through Greenwich, London. Equator — 0° latitude (dividing N/S hemispheres). Tropic of Cancer — 23.5° N. International Date Line — approximately 180° longitude (zig-zags to avoid splitting countries).

cards.front:
The 'Tibetan Plateau' — the highest and largest plateau in the world — lies chiefly in:

(A) India
(B) China (Tibet)
(C) Nepal
(D) Bhutan
cards.back:
(B) China (Tibet)

World Geography — Tibetan Plateau — also called the 'Roof of the World' — average elevation > 4,500 m; area ~2.5 million km². Mostly in China's Tibet Autonomous Region and Qinghai Province. cards.front:
The 'Deccan Plateau' of peninsular India is bordered by:

(A) Himalayas on the north
(B) Satpura hills on the north, Western and Eastern Ghats on the sides
(C) Aravallis on all sides
(D) Vindhyas on the south
cards.back:
(B) Satpura hills on the north, Western and Eastern Ghats on the sides

World Geography — Deccan Plateau — roughly triangular. Northern edge — Satpura hills (with the Vindhyas just beyond, north of Narmada). Western edge — Western Ghats (rising up from the Arabian Sea coast). Eastern edge — Eastern Ghats (lower, more broken). The plateau tilts gently eastward — which is why major peninsular rivers (Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri) flow east to the Bay of Bengal.

The 'Colorado Plateau' — famous for the Grand Canyon — lies in:

(B) United States
(C) Mexico

The Colorado River has carved the Grand Canyon (~1.6 km deep) across this plateau over 5-6 million years. Other famous US landmarks here — Monument Valley, Bryce Canyon, Zion, Mesa Verde.

The Chota Nagpur plateau is a major source of minerals in India — especially:

(A) Petroleum and natural gas
(B) Coal and iron ore
(C) Gold and silver
(D) Uranium and thorium only
cards.back:
(B) Coal and iron ore

World Geography — Chota Nagpur Plateau (Jharkhand, parts of Chhattisgarh, Odisha, WB) — India's 'mineral storehouse'. The Damodar river (Bengal's 'sorrow' before the Damodar Valley Corporation dams) flows through it. Petroleum is chiefly offshore (Mumbai High) and in Assam.

cards.front:
A plateau formed by extensive lava flows is called a:

(A) Piedmont plateau
(B) Volcanic (lava) plateau
(C) Continental plateau
(D) Intermontane plateau
cards.back:
(B) Volcanic (lava) plateau

World Geography — Volcanic / lava plateaus form when lava flows from many fissures cover a large area and solidify. Example — Deccan Traps (India) — huge lava plateau laid down ~65 million years ago, some theories linking it to the K-Pg mass extinction; Columbia River Plateau (USA); Drakensberg in Ethiopia. Piedmont plateau — 'at the foot of mountains' (e.g., near the Appalachians). Intermontane — between mountains (e.g., Tibet, between Himalayas and Kunlun).

cards.front:
The longest river in the world is the:

(A) Amazon
(B) Nile
(C) Yangtze
(D) Mississippi
cards.back:
(B) Nile

World Geography — The Nile, at about 6,650 km, is generally taken as the world's longest river. Some recent surveys have put the Amazon very close (~6,400-6,800 km) and the question is still debated among geographers, but standard exam textbooks treat the Nile as No. 1. Yangtze (~6,300 km) is Asia's longest; the Mississippi-Missouri system is North America's longest.

Its source is in the Peruvian Andes; it empties into the Atlantic in Brazil. The Congo is the second-largest by discharge.

cards.front:
The rivers Tigris and Euphrates together formed the cradle of which ancient civilisation?

(A) Egyptian
(B) Mesopotamian
(C) Indus Valley
(D) Chinese (Huang He)
cards.back:
(B) Mesopotamian

Egypt grew along the Nile; the Indus Valley along the Indus and Ghaggar-Hakra; ancient Chinese civilisation along the Huang He (Yellow River).

cards.front:
Which is the LARGEST Scheduled Tribe by population in India (Census 2011)?

(A) Gond tribe of central India
(B) Bhil tribe of western India
(C) Santhal tribe of eastern India
(D) Munda tribe of Chota Nagpur
cards.back:
(A) Gond tribe of central India

Indian Tribes & People — GOND TRIBE — largest Scheduled Tribe in India (~1.22 crore as per Census 2011). They inhabit the CENTRAL INDIAN HIGHLANDS — the historical 'Gondwana' region — spread across MADHYA PRADESH, MAHARASHTRA, CHHATTISGARH, TELANGANA, ANDHRA PRADESH, ODISHA. The supercontinent 'GONDWANA' is named after them (geological term coined by Eduard Suess, 1885). LANGUAGE: Gondi (Dravidian family). CULTURE: famous for Gond paintings (Jangarh Singh Shyam pioneered the modern style). RANKING — TOP TRIBES BY POPULATION: (1) Gond ~1.22 cr. (2) BHIL ~1.04 cr (Rajasthan, MP, Gujarat, Maharashtra). (3) SANTHAL ~70 lakh (Jharkhand, WB, Odisha). (4) MEENA ~50 lakh (Rajasthan, MP). (5) MUNDA ~22 lakh (Jharkhand). KEY STATS: total ST population ~10.45 crore (8.6% of India). Madhya Pradesh has the LARGEST ST population in absolute numbers; MIZORAM and NAGALAND are HIGHEST in PERCENTAGE (>90% tribal). LAKSHADWEEP has 95% ST population. PYQ FREQUENCY: 'largest tribe in India' is a 1-mark guarantee in SSC CGL, IBPS GA, RRB. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests tribal-population-distribution recall.

(A) President of India via notification
(B) Parliament with simple majority law
(C) National Commission for STs (NCST)
(D) State legislature on its own there
cards.back:
(A) President of India via notification

Indian Tribes & People — ARTICLE 342 (Scheduled Tribes): the PRESIDENT OF INDIA, after CONSULTATION WITH THE GOVERNOR of the state, may by PUBLIC NOTIFICATION specify the tribes/communities deemed Scheduled Tribes for that state/UT. PARLIAMENT may then INCLUDE or EXCLUDE any tribe from this list by simple-majority law (ordinary legislation, not constitutional amendment). ARTICLE 341 mirrors this for Scheduled Castes. RESERVATION POLICY: STs get 7.5% reservation in central govt jobs, education, and proportionate share in legislatures. CRITERIA used by Lokur Committee (1965) for ST classification: (1) Indications of primitive traits. (2) Distinctive culture. (3) Geographic isolation. (4) Shyness of contact with outside community. (5) Backwardness. CONSTITUTIONAL SAFEGUARDS: Art 15(4), 16(4), 46, 244, 275, 330, 332, 335, 338A, 339, 342. NATIONAL COMMISSION FOR SCHEDULED TRIBES (NCST) — Art 338A, established 2004 (89th Amendment) by bifurcating the earlier joint SC-ST Commission. PYQ FREQUENCY: Art 341/342 distinction tested in UPSC, MPSC, CGL Tier-2.

cards.front:
The SANTHAL REBELLION ('HUL') of 1855 against British colonial rule was led by:

(A) Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu (brothers)
(B) Birsa Munda with his followers
(C) Tilka Manjhi and Paharia tribes
(D) Tantya Bhil and Bhagoji Naik
cards.back:
(A) Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu (brothers)

Indian Tribes & People — SANTHAL REBELLION (SANTHAL HUL) 1855 — one of India's earliest organized tribal uprisings against British colonial rule, zamindars, and exploitative moneylenders ('dikus'). LEADERS: SIDHU MURMU and KANHU MURMU — brothers from BHOGNADIH village (Sahibganj district, present-day Jharkhand). Two more brothers — Chand and Bhairav — also led contingents. Mobilized ~60,000 Santhals; declared independence on 30 JUNE 1855 (now observed as 'Hul Diwas' in Jharkhand). British retaliation: martial law; ~15,000-20,000 Santhals killed; Sidhu and Kanhu captured and hanged. OUTCOME — SANTAL PARGANAS TENANCY ACT, 1876: granted Santhal farmers protection from land alienation; the area still has a separate tenancy regime. 'HUL' = revolution in Santali language (Ol Chiki script). CONTRAST WITH OTHER TRIBAL REVOLTS: (1) BIRSA MUNDA's 'ULGULAN' (1899-1900) — Munda tribe in Chota Nagpur against missionaries+British; Birsa is 'Dharti Abba' (Father of Earth). (2) TILKA MANJHI (1780s) — earlier Paharia revolt. (3) TANTYA BHIL (late 19th c.) — Bhil chief, Robin-Hood figure of central India. (4) RAMPA REBELLION 1922 — Alluri Sitarama Raju, Andhra Koya tribes. PYQ ANGLE: tribal revolts perennial UPSC, SSC topic.

cards.front:
WARLI PAINTINGS — the famous monochrome tribal art form — originate from which state?

(A) Maharashtra (Thane, Nashik area)
(B) Madhya Pradesh tribal belt also
(C) Jharkhand (Santal Parganas zone)
(D) Gujarat (Dang district region)
cards.back:
(A) Maharashtra (Thane, Nashik area)

Indian Tribes & People — WARLI PAINTING — visual art of the WARLI TRIBE living in the THANE, PALGHAR, NASHIK districts of MAHARASHTRA (and small communities in adjoining Gujarat & Dadra-Nagar-Haveli). STYLE: monochrome (white rice-paste motifs on RED-OCHRE mud walls) using simple geometric shapes — TRIANGLES (humans, mountains), CIRCLES (sun, moon), SQUARES (sacred enclosure), spirals. THEMES: harvest, hunting, wedding, fertility rites, daily life. RECOGNITION: granted GEOGRAPHICAL INDICATION (GI) tag in 2014; works displayed in major global museums. KEY ARTIST: JIVYA SOMA MASHE (Padma Shri 2011) — credited with bringing Warli art into the modern public sphere. OTHER MAJOR TRIBAL/FOLK ART FORMS (memorize for SSC/UPSC GA): (1) GOND PAINTING — MP (vibrant dots-and-lines, animals, mythology). (2) PITHORA — Bhil/Rathwa tribes, Gujarat (ritual marriage art). (3) SAURA — Odisha (Lanjia Saura tribe). (4) MADHUBANI — Bihar (Mithila region). (5) PATTACHITRA — Odisha/WB. (6) KALAMKARI — Andhra Pradesh. PYQ FREQUENCY: tribal-art-state mapping is a top SSC, UPSC, IBPS GA MCQ — 1-2× per cycle.

cards.front:
The SIXTH SCHEDULE of the Constitution provides for Autonomous District Councils in:

(A) Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram
(B) Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha
(C) Nagaland, Manipur, and Arunachal
(D) All states with Fifth Schedule areas
cards.back:
(A) Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram

Indian Tribes & People — SIXTH SCHEDULE (Articles 244(2), 275(1)): provides for AUTONOMOUS DISTRICT COUNCILS (ADCs) and Regional Councils in tribal areas of FOUR NORTHEASTERN STATES — ASSAM, MEGHALAYA, TRIPURA, MIZORAM. ADCs have LEGISLATIVE (laws on land, forests, marriage, inheritance), JUDICIAL (intra-tribe disputes), and FINANCIAL powers within their territories. CURRENT ADCs: ASSAM — North Cachar Hills (Dima Hasao), Karbi Anglong, Bodoland Territorial Council (BTC). MEGHALAYA — Khasi Hills, Jaintia Hills, Garo Hills ADCs. TRIPURA — Tripura Tribal Areas ADC. MIZORAM — Chakma, Mara, Lai ADCs. FIFTH SCHEDULE (Article 244(1)): covers Scheduled Areas in NINE OTHER STATES — Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha. KEY CONTRAST: Fifth Schedule = administered by Governor with TAC (Tribes Advisory Council); Sixth Schedule = elected ADCs with autonomous law-making. RECENT: Ladakh demand for Sixth Schedule status (Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike, March 2024) — government has not yet granted. PYQ FREQUENCY: Fifth vs Sixth Schedule distinction is top-5 polity MCQ in UPSC, MPSC, NEET-style civics.
cards.option3: All states with Fifth Schedule areas

cards.front:
Which of these tribes is classified as a PARTICULARLY VULNERABLE TRIBAL GROUP (PVTG)?

(A) Jarawa of the Andaman Islands
(B) Gond of Madhya Pradesh region
(C) Bhil of Rajasthan-MP-Gujarat belt
(D) Santhal of the Santal Parganas
cards.back:
(A) Jarawa of the Andaman Islands

Indian Tribes & People — PARTICULARLY VULNERABLE TRIBAL GROUPS (PVTGs) — formerly called 'Primitive Tribal Groups' (PTGs); renamed in 2006 by Ministry of Tribal Affairs based on Xaxa Committee (2004) recommendations. CRITERIA: (1) Pre-agricultural level of technology (hunting-gathering). (2) Stagnant or declining population. (3) Very low literacy. (4) Subsistence-level economy. NUMBERS: 75 PVTGs identified across 18 states/UTs. NOTABLE PVTGs: (a) JARAWA — Andaman, ~250-400 members; live in 1,028 sq km reserve; the 'Andaman Trunk Road' controversy (cuts through their territory). (b) GREAT ANDAMANESE — ~50 survivors; severely endangered. (c) ONGE — Little Andaman, ~120. (d) SHOMPEN — Great Nicobar, ~200. (e) SENTINELESE — completely isolated; refused all contact; the John Allen Chau incident (Nov 2018, US missionary killed). (f) DONGRIA KONDH — Niyamgiri Hills, Odisha; landmark 2013 Supreme Court Vedanta case where Gram Sabhas vetoed bauxite mining. (g) CHENCHU — AP/Telangana, hunter-gatherers. (h) BIRHOR, ASUR — Jharkhand. (i) BAIGA — MP. SCHEMES: PVTG Development Mission, Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN, ₹24,104 cr launched Nov 2023). PYQ ANGLE: PVTG names + locations frequent in UPSC, SSC.

cards.front:
The PESA Act, 1996 is significant for tribal areas because it:

(A) Extends Panchayati Raj to Fifth Schedule areas
(B) Reserves seats for tribals in state cabinets
(C) Grants tribals exemption from income tax
(D) Sets up separate tribal courts in districts
cards.back:
(A) Extends Panchayati Raj to Fifth Schedule areas

Indian Tribes & People — PESA = PANCHAYATS (EXTENSION TO SCHEDULED AREAS) ACT, 1996. CONTEXT: the 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992) extended Panchayati Raj to rural India — but EXCLUDED Fifth Schedule areas (tribal regions of 9 states). PESA filled this gap by EXTENDING Panchayati Raj provisions to FIFTH SCHEDULE AREAS, with safeguards for tribal traditions. KEY PROVISIONS: (1) GRAM SABHA = supreme decision-making body for tribal villages (NOT just Panchayat). (2) Gram Sabha consent REQUIRED for: land acquisition, mineral concessions, rehabilitation, minor forest produce management, minor water bodies. (3) Tribes Advisory Council oversees implementation. (4) No outsider can be granted exclusive rights over minor forest produce. (5) Power to prevent land alienation. (6) Reservation for STs in panchayats proportionate to population. STATES COVERED (9): Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha. CHALLENGE: weak implementation — many states have not yet notified PESA Rules. COMPLEMENTARY ACT: FOREST RIGHTS ACT, 2006 (FRA) — recognizes individual + community forest rights of tribes inhabiting forest land. PYQ FREQUENCY: PESA is a top-3 tribal-governance MCQ in UPSC, HJS, state PSC.

cards.option2: Grants tribals exemption from income tax
cards.option3: Sets up separate tribal courts in districts
